headings.text: Grace and peace to the seven churches

verses.text: The revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants the things that must soon happen; and He made it known by signs, sending it through His angel to His servant John,
verses.note: Gr. δούλοις, lit. “slaves”. “Made it known by signs”: Gr. ἐσήμανεν, a verb related to σημεῖον, “sign”; the book communicates through symbols.

verses.text: who testified to the Word of God and the Testimony of Jesus Christ, all that he saw.
verses.note: The μαρτυρ- family is always rendered testify / testimony / Witness (cf. 12:17; 19:10).

verses.text: Blessed is the one who reads, and those who hear the words of the prophecy and keep what is written in it, for the time is near.
verses.note: A single “blessed” (μακάριος) covers the reader, in the singular (the one who reads aloud in the assembly), and a single group that hears and keeps; one article governs both participles. τηρέω = “keep” throughout the book (cf. 12:17; 14:12).

verses.text: John, to the seven churches that are in Asia: Grace to you and peace from Him Who Is, and Who Was, and Who Is Coming, and from the Seven Spirits who are before His throne,
verses.note: Gr. ἀπὸ ὁ ὤν: the divine name stays in the nominative after the preposition, as an indeclinable name (cf. Ex 3:14). “Who Is Coming”: present tense (ὁ ἐρχόμενος), the same verb as “He is coming” in 1:7. “Seven Spirits”: the capital follows their place in the greeting, between Him Who Is and Jesus Christ, as the source of grace and peace; alternative reading: seven angelic spirits (cf. 8:2).

verses.text: and from Jesus Christ, the faithful Witness, the Firstborn of the dead, and the Ruler of the kings of the earth. To Him who loves us and freed us from our sins by His blood,
verses.note: Variants: the Textus Receptus reads “loved us”; it and the Byzantine text read “washed us” (λούσαντι). The SBLGNT is followed, with Papyrus 18 and codices Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Ephraemi: “loves us” (ἀγαπῶντι) and “freed us” (λύσαντι).

verses.text: and made us a kingdom, priests to His God and Father, to Him be the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
verses.note: Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “kings and priests”; the SBLGNT, “a kingdom, priests” (cf. Ex 19:6). “Forever and ever” (εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, lit. “to the ages of the ages”): the formula is rendered the same way throughout the book.

verses.text: Behold, He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him, and also those who pierced Him; and all the tribes of the earth will mourn over Him. Yes, amen.
verses.note: Cf. Dan 7:13; Zech 12:10. “Yes, amen”: Gr. ναί (Greek) + ἀμήν (Hebrew), a double affirmation.

verses.text: I am the Alpha and the Omega, says the Lord God, He Who Is, and Who Was, and Who Is Coming, the Almighty.
verses.note: “Almighty”: Gr. παντοκράτωρ, which in the Septuagint usually renders “LORD of Hosts” (e.g. Amos 4:13) and, in Job, “Shaddai”. Variant: the Textus Receptus adds “the Beginning and the End” and reads “says the Lord”, without “God”.

verses.text: I, John, your brother and companion in the tribulation and the kingdom and the perseverance in Jesus, was on the island called Patmos because of the Word of God and the Testimony of Jesus.
verses.note: “Was” renders ἐγενόμην, a verb repeated in 1:9, 1:10 and 1:18. ὑπομονή = “perseverance” (cf. 14:12). Variant: the Byzantine text reads “in Christ Jesus”, and the Textus Receptus “of Jesus Christ”; both read “the Testimony of Jesus Christ”.

verses.text: I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day, and I heard behind me a loud voice like a trumpet,
verses.note: Gr. ἐν τῇ κυριακῇ ἡμέρᾳ, with the adjective κυριακός, “belonging to the Lord”; the text does not name the day. Cf. Ex 20:10; Isa 58:13; Mark 2:28.

verses.text: saying: What you see, write in a book, and send it to the seven churches: to Ephesus, and to Smyrna, and to Pergamum, and to Thyatira, and to Sardis, and to Philadelphia, and to Laodicea.
verses.note: Gr. βιβλίον, a scroll; “book” is kept for consistency with 5:1ff. Variant: the Textus Receptus begins the speech with “I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last” and adds “that are in Asia”.

verses.text: And I turned to see the voice that was speaking with me, and when I turned I saw seven golden lampstands,
verses.note: Gr. λυχνία; cf. the lampstand of the sanctuary, Ex 25:31–37.

verses.text: and in the midst of the lampstands One like a Son of Man, clothed in a robe reaching to the feet and girded at the chest with a golden sash.
verses.note: Cf. Dan 7:13; “a Son of Man”: Gr. υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου, without the article, as in Daniel. “Robe reaching to the feet”: Gr. ποδήρη, the term for the high priest’s garments in the Septuagint (Ex 28:4; 28:31 [LXX 28:27]; cf. Zech 3:4). The capital follows the self-identification in 1:17–18. Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “the seven lampstands”.

verses.text: His head and hair were white like white wool, like snow; and His eyes were like a flame of fire;
verses.note: Cf. Dan 7:9 (the Ancient of Days).

verses.text: His feet were like gleaming bronze, as though refined in a furnace; and His voice was like the voice of many waters.
verses.note: Gr. χαλκολίβανον, a metal of uncertain identification. “Refined”: the same verb as in 3:18 (πυρόω). Cf. Ezek 43:2.

verses.text: In His right hand He held seven stars, and out of His mouth came a sharp two-edged sword; and His face was like the sun when it shines in its strength.
verses.note: Cf. Isa 49:2; Judg 5:31.

verses.text: When I saw Him, I fell at His feet as one dead. Then He laid His right hand on me, saying: Do not fear; I am the First and the Last,
verses.note: “Right hand”: Gr. τὴν δεξιάν, “the right”, without the word “hand” (also in 1:20); in 1:16 the Greek has “right hand”. Variant: the Textus Receptus adds “hand” here. Cf. Isa 44:6; 48:12.

verses.text: and the Living One. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever, and I have the keys of death and of the grave.
verses.note: “The grave”: Gr. ᾅδης (Hades), equivalent to Heb. sheol (cf. Hos 13:14). Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus add “Amen” after “forever and ever”; the Textus Receptus reads “of the grave and of death”.

verses.text: Write, therefore, the things that you saw, and the things that are, and the things that are about to happen after these things.
verses.note: Or: “the things that you saw, that is, the things that are and the things that are about to happen after these things”.

verses.text: As for the mystery of the seven stars that you saw in My right hand, and of the seven golden lampstands: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.
verses.note: Gr. ἄγγελοι, or “messengers”.

segments.text: The revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants the things that must soon happen; and He made it known by signs, sending it through His angel to His servant John,
who testified to the Word of God and the Testimony of Jesus Christ, all that he saw.
Blessed is the one who reads, and those who hear the words of the prophecy and keep what is written in it, for the time is near.

blocks.text: Grace and peace to the seven churches

segments.text: John, to the seven churches that are in Asia:
Grace to you and peace
from Him Who Is, and Who Was, and Who Is Coming,
and from the Seven Spirits who are before His throne,
and from Jesus Christ, the faithful Witness, the Firstborn of the dead, and the Ruler of the kings of the earth.
To Him who loves us
and freed us from our sins by His blood,
and made us a kingdom, priests to His God and Father,
to Him be the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
Behold, He is coming with the clouds,
and every eye will see Him,
and also those who pierced Him;
and all the tribes of the earth will mourn over Him.
Yes, amen.
I am the Alpha and the Omega, says the Lord God,
He Who Is, and Who Was, and Who Is Coming, the Almighty.
I, John, your brother and companion in the tribulation and the kingdom and the perseverance in Jesus, was on the island called Patmos because of the Word of God and the Testimony of Jesus.
I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day, and I heard behind me a loud voice like a trumpet,
saying: What you see, write in a book, and send it to the seven churches: to Ephesus, and to Smyrna, and to Pergamum, and to Thyatira, and to Sardis, and to Philadelphia, and to Laodicea.
And I turned to see the voice that was speaking with me, and when I turned I saw seven golden lampstands,
and in the midst of the lampstands One like a Son of Man, clothed in a robe reaching to the feet and girded at the chest with a golden sash.
His head and hair were white like white wool, like snow;
and His eyes were like a flame of fire;
His feet were like gleaming bronze, as though refined in a furnace;
and His voice was like the voice of many waters.
In His right hand He held seven stars,
and out of His mouth came a sharp two-edged sword;
and His face was like the sun when it shines in its strength.
When I saw Him, I fell at His feet as one dead. Then He laid His right hand on me, saying: Do not fear; I am the First and the Last,
and the Living One. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever, and I have the keys of death and of the grave.
Write, therefore, the things that you saw, and the things that are, and the things that are about to happen after these things.

As for the mystery of the seven stars that you saw in My right hand, and of the seven golden lampstands: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.

verses.text: To the angel of the church in Ephesus write: Thus says He who holds the seven stars in His right hand, He who walks in the midst of the seven golden lampstands:
verses.note: “Angel”: Gr. ἄγγελος, or “messenger” (cf. 1:20). “Thus says”: Gr. τάδε λέγει, the prophetic formula of the Septuagint (“Thus says the LORD”), repeated in all seven letters. “Holds”: Gr. κρατῶν, from κρατέω, “to hold firmly”.

verses.text: I know your works, your toil and your perseverance, and that you cannot bear those who are evil; you have tested those who call themselves apostles, and are not, and have found them liars;
verses.note: “Toil”: Gr. κόπος, “wearying toil”; the related verb appears in 2:3 (“have not grown weary”).

verses.text: and you have perseverance, and have borne up for My name’s sake, and have not grown weary.
But I have this against you: you have left your first love.
Remember, then, from where you have fallen, and repent, and do the first works; and if not, I am coming to you and will move your lampstand from its place, unless you repent.
verses.note: Gr. κινήσω, “move, remove from its place”; the lampstand is the church (1:20). “Have fallen”: perfect (πέπτωκας), a fall whose state remains. Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus add “quickly” after “I am coming to you”.

verses.text: But this you have: you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
verses.note: The Nicolaitans are mentioned only in Revelation (cf. 2:15).

verses.text: Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who conquers I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God.
verses.note: “To the one who conquers” (νικῶντι): νικάω = “conquer” in all seven letters. Gr. ξύλον, “wood, tree”, the term of Gen 2:9 (Septuagint), also used in the New Testament for the cross (Acts 5:30); cf. 22:2, 14. Variant: the Byzantine text reads “the paradise of My God”; the Textus Receptus, “in the midst of the paradise of God”.

verses.text: And to the angel of the church in Smyrna write: Thus says the First and the Last, who was dead and came to life:
verses.note: “Was dead”: Gr. ἐγένετο νεκρός, as in 1:18 (“I was dead”). “Came to life”: Gr. ἔζησεν, the same verb as in 20:4–5.

verses.text: I know your tribulation and your poverty (but you are rich), and the blasphemy of those who say they are Jews, and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.
verses.note: Or “slander” (Gr. βλασφημία). The expression does not refer to the Jewish people as such, but to those who, according to the text itself, “say they are Jews, and are not” (cf. 3:9; Rom 2:28–29). Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus begin “I know your works, and your tribulation”.

verses.text: Do not fear anything that you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to cast some of you into prison, that you may be tested, and you will have tribulation for ten days. Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life.
verses.note: “Tested”: Gr. πειρασθῆτε, the same verb as in 2:2 (“you have tested”). “Ten days”: cf. Dan 1:12, 14. “Crown”: Gr. στέφανος, the victor’s wreath, distinct from διάδημα, “diadem” (12:3; 13:1; 19:12).

verses.text: Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. The one who conquers will by no means be harmed by the second death.
verses.note: Gr. οὐ μή, an emphatic negation. Second death: cf. 20:6, 14; 21:8.

verses.text: And to the angel of the church in Pergamum write: Thus says He who has the sharp two-edged sword:

I know where you dwell: where the throne of Satan is. And you hold fast My name, and you did not deny My faith, even in the days of Antipas, My witness, My faithful one, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells.
verses.note: “Hold fast”: Gr. κρατέω, the same verb as in 2:1 (“holds”), 2:14–15 (“hold”) and 2:25 (“hold fast”). “My faith”: or “faith in Me” (cf. 14:12). “Witness”: Gr. μάρτυς, the same word as in 1:5, which later gave “martyr”. “Dwell… dwells”: the same verb (κατοικέω). Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus begin “I know your works and where you dwell”.

verses.text: But I have a few things against you: you have there those who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to cast a stumbling block before the sons of Israel, so that they would eat food sacrificed to idols and prostitute themselves.
verses.note: Cf. Num 25:1–3; 31:16. “Teaching… taught”: Gr. διδαχή / ἐδίδασκεν. “Stumbling block”: Gr. σκάνδαλον. “Prostitute themselves”: Gr. πορνεύω; in Num 25:1 the Hebrew uses זָנָה‎, “to prostitute oneself”, linked to idolatry; in Revelation the term joins sexual and spiritual unfaithfulness (cf. 17:1–2).

verses.text: So you also have those who likewise hold the teaching of the Nicolaitans.
verses.note: Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “which I hate” in place of “likewise”.

verses.text: Repent, then; and if not, I am coming to you soon and will make war against them with the sword of My mouth.

Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who conquers I will give some of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white pebble, and on the pebble a new name written, which no one knows except the one who receives it.
verses.note: Hidden manna: cf. Ex 16:33–34. “Pebble”: Gr. ψῆφος, a small stone used in voting and as a token of admission. “New”: Gr. καινός (cf. 3:12; 21:1, 5). “Knows”: the same verb as “I know” (οἶδα).

verses.text: And to the angel of the church in Thyatira write: Thus says the Son of God, who has His eyes like a flame of fire and His feet like gleaming bronze:
I know your works, and your love, and faith, and service, and perseverance; and your last works are more than the first.
verses.note: Or: “I know your works, that is, your love, and faith…”.

verses.text: But I have this against you: you tolerate the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, and she teaches and deceives My servants to prostitute themselves and to eat food sacrificed to idols.
verses.note: “Tolerate”: Gr. ἀφεῖς, the same verb as in 2:4 (“have left”). “Woman”: Gr. γυνή, also “wife”; variant: the Byzantine text reads “your wife Jezebel”, and the Textus Receptus “I have a few things against you”. “Deceives”: Gr. πλανάω (cf. 12:9; 13:14; 20:3, 8, 10). Cf. 1 Kgs 16:31.

verses.text: And I gave her time to repent, and she is not willing to repent of her prostitution.
Behold, I am casting her onto a bed, and those who commit adultery with her into great tribulation, unless they repent of her works;
verses.note: “Bed”: Gr. κλίνη, also a sickbed. “Great tribulation”: cf. 7:14. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “of their works”.

verses.text: and I will kill her children with pestilence; and all the churches will know that I am He who searches minds and hearts, and I will give to each one of you according to your works.
verses.note: “With pestilence”: Gr. ἐν θανάτῳ, lit. “with death”; in the Septuagint θάνατος often renders Heb. דֶּבֶר‎, “pestilence” (cf. 6:8; 18:8; Ezek 5:12; 33:27). “Minds”: Gr. νεφροί, lit. “kidneys”, in Hebrew thought the seat of the emotions and conscience (Jer 17:10, Heb. כְּלָיוֹת‎).

verses.text: But to you I say, to the remnant in Thyatira, all who do not have this teaching, who have not known the depths of Satan, as they say: I do not cast on you any other burden;
verses.note: “Remnant”: Gr. λοιποί, “those who remain”; the same word as in 12:17. Where it designates other groups (9:20; 19:21; 20:5), it is rendered “the rest”. “Burden”: Gr. βάρος, cf. Acts 15:28–29. “Depths”: cf. 1 Cor 2:10.

verses.text: only, what you have, hold fast until I come.
The one who conquers and keeps My works until the end, to him I will give authority over the nations,
verses.note: “Keeps”: Gr. τηρέω (cf. 1:3). “Nations”: Gr. ἔθνη.

verses.text: and he will shepherd them with a rod of iron, as clay vessels are shattered,
verses.note: Cf. Ps 2:8–9. “Shepherd”: Gr. ποιμαίνω, “to tend as a shepherd”, as in the Septuagint of Ps 2:9; the Hebrew reads “you will break” (תְּרֹעֵם‎). Cf. 7:17; 12:5; 19:15.

verses.text: even as I also have received from My Father; and I will give him the morning star.
Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

And to the angel of the church in Smyrna write:
Thus says the First and the Last,
who was dead and came to life:
I know your tribulation and your poverty (but you are rich), and the blasphemy of those who say they are Jews, and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.

Thus says He who has the sharp two-edged sword:

I know where you dwell: where the throne of Satan is. And you hold fast My name, and you did not deny My faith, even in the days of Antipas, My witness, My faithful one, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells.

But I have a few things against you: you have there those who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to cast a stumbling block before the sons of Israel, so that they would eat food sacrificed to idols and prostitute themselves.
So you also have those who likewise hold the teaching of the Nicolaitans.
Repent, then; and if not, I am coming to you soon and will make war against them with the sword of My mouth.

Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who conquers I will give some of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white pebble, and on the pebble a new name written, which no one knows except the one who receives it.
And to the angel of the church in Thyatira write:
Thus says the Son of God,
who has His eyes like a flame of fire
and His feet like gleaming bronze:
I know your works, and your love, and faith, and service, and perseverance; and your last works are more than the first.
But I have this against you: you tolerate the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, and she teaches and deceives My servants to prostitute themselves and to eat food sacrificed to idols.
And I gave her time to repent, and she is not willing to repent of her prostitution.
Behold, I am casting her onto a bed, and those who commit adultery with her into great tribulation, unless they repent of her works;
and I will kill her children with pestilence; and all the churches will know that I am He who searches minds and hearts, and I will give to each one of you according to your works.
But to you I say, to the remnant in Thyatira, all who do not have this teaching, who have not known the depths of Satan, as they say: I do not cast on you any other burden;
only, what you have, hold fast until I come.

and he will shepherd them with a rod of iron, as clay vessels are shattered,
even as I also have received from My Father; and I will give him the morning star.
Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

verses.text: And to the angel of the church in Sardis write: Thus says He who has the Seven Spirits of God and the seven stars: I know your works, that you have a name of being alive, and you are dead.
verses.note: “Seven Spirits”: cf. 1:4. “A name of being alive”: Gr. ὄνομα ἔχεις ὅτι ζῇς, lit. “a name that you live”; “name”, that is, reputation; the word recurs in 3:4–5.

verses.text: Be watchful, and strengthen the things that remain, which were about to die; for I have not found your works complete before My God.
verses.note: “Be watchful”: Gr. γίνου γρηγορῶν, like “Be faithful” (2:10); γρηγορέω = “watch” (3:3; 16:15). “The things that remain”: Gr. τὰ λοιπά (plural). Variant: the Byzantine text reads “which you were about to throw away” (ἔμελλες ἀποβάλλειν); the Textus Receptus reads “which is about to die” (μέλλει, singular and present) and “before God”, without “My”.

verses.text: Remember, then, how you have received and heard, and keep it, and repent. If, then, you do not watch, I will come like a thief, and you will by no means know at what hour I will come upon you.
verses.note: “Like a thief”: cf. 16:15; Matt 24:43; 1 Thess 5:2. “I will come”: Gr. ἥξω, as in 2:25 (“until I come”). “By no means”: Gr. οὐ μή, an emphatic negation. Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “I will come upon you like a thief”.

verses.text: But you have a few names in Sardis who have not defiled their garments, and they will walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.
verses.note: “Names”: that is, persons (cf. Acts 1:15); a wordplay with “name” in 3:1 and 3:5. “Garments”: Gr. ἱμάτια (cf. 3:5, 18; 16:15). “Defiled”: Gr. μολύνω (cf. 14:4).

verses.text: The one who conquers will thus be clothed in white garments, and I will by no means blot out his name from the book of life, and I will confess his name before My Father and before His angels.
verses.note: “Book of life”: cf. Ex 32:32–33; Dan 12:1; Phil 4:3; Rev 13:8; 20:12, 15. “Blot out”: Gr. ἐξαλείφω, the same verb as in 7:17 and 21:4 (“wipe away”). Cf. Matt 10:32. Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “this one will be clothed” (οὗτος) in place of “will thus be clothed” (οὕτως).

verses.text: Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write: Thus says the Holy One, the True One, He who has the key of David, who opens, and no one will shut, and shuts, and no one opens:
verses.note: Cf. Isa 22:22. “True One”: Gr. ἀληθινός (cf. 3:14; 19:11). Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “and no one shuts, and shuts, and no one opens” (κλείει, present, in both places); the Byzantine text, “and no one will shut it except the one who opens, and no one will open”.

verses.text: I know your works (behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one is able to shut), that you have little power, and you have kept My word, and have not denied My name.
verses.note: “Set”: Gr. δέδωκα, lit. “I have given”. “That you have”: or “because you have”. “Power”: Gr. δύναμις (cf. 4:11; 5:12).

verses.text: Behold, I am handing over some of the synagogue of Satan, of those who say they are Jews, and are not, but lie; behold, I will make them come and bow down before your feet, and know that I loved you.
verses.note: “Handing over”: Gr. διδῶ, lit. “I give”; the Greek sentence breaks off and starts again (“behold, I will make them…”). “Bow down”: Gr. προσκυνέω, the verb rendered “worship” when the object is God (cf. 4:10; 14:7); here, homage (cf. Isa 60:14 Heb.; 45:14; 49:23). On “synagogue of Satan”, cf. 2:9.

verses.text: Because you have kept the word of My perseverance, I also will keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole world, to test those who dwell on the earth.
verses.note: “Kept… keep”: the same verb (τηρέω). “The word of My perseverance”: or “My word about perseverance”. “Testing… test”: Gr. πειρασμός / πειράζω (cf. πειράζω in 2:2, 10). “The whole world”: Gr. οἰκουμένη ὅλη, lit. “the whole inhabited world” (cf. 12:9). “Those who dwell on the earth”: a recurring formula (cf. 6:10; 13:8).

verses.text: I am coming soon; hold fast what you have, so that no one takes your crown.
verses.note: “Soon”: Gr. ταχύ (cf. 2:16). “Hold fast”: Gr. κρατέω (cf. 2:25). “Crown”: Gr. στέφανος (cf. 2:10). Variant: the Textus Receptus begins “Behold, I am coming soon”.

verses.text: The one who conquers, I will make him a pillar in the sanctuary of My God, and he will by no means go out of it again; and I will write on him the name of My God, and the name of the city of My God, the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God, and My new name.
verses.note: “Sanctuary”: Gr. ναός, the inner part of the temple, distinct from ἱερόν, the whole temple complex; in Revelation, always ναός (cf. 7:15; 11:19; 15:5). “New Jerusalem”: cf. 21:2. “New name”: cf. 2:17; Isa 62:2.

verses.text: Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
And to the angel of the church in Laodicea write: Thus says the Amen, the faithful and true Witness, the Beginning of the creation of God:
verses.note: “The Amen”: cf. Isa 65:16 (Heb. “the God of amen”; Septuagint “the true God”). “Beginning”: Gr. ἀρχή, “beginning, origin” or “ruler”; the same term used as a title in 21:6 and 22:13 (“the Beginning and the End”). Cf. John 1:3; Col 1:15–18.

verses.text: I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot. Would that you were cold or hot!
verses.note: “Hot”: Gr. ζεστός, lit. “boiling”.

verses.text: So, because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I am about to vomit you out of My mouth.
verses.note: “Am about to”: Gr. μέλλω (cf. 1:19; 2:10).

verses.text: Because you say: I am rich, and have grown rich, and have need of nothing; and you do not know that it is you who are wretched, and pitiable, and poor, and blind, and naked,
verses.note: “Have grown rich”: perfect (πεπλούτηκα), “I have become rich” (a state that remains).

verses.text: I counsel you to buy from Me gold refined by fire, so that you may be rich; and white garments, so that you may clothe yourself and the shame of your nakedness may not be made manifest; and eye salve to anoint your eyes, so that you may see.
verses.note: “Refined”: Gr. πυρόω (cf. 1:15). “Clothe yourself”: Gr. περιβάλλω, the same verb as in 3:5 (“clothed”).

verses.text: As for Me, all whom I love I rebuke and discipline; be zealous, then, and repent.
verses.note: “Love”: Gr. φιλέω. Cf. Prov 3:12 (Septuagint, with the same verb “rebuke”).

verses.text: Behold, I stand at the door and knock; if anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and dine with him, and he with Me.
verses.note: “Stand”: perfect (ἕστηκα), “I have taken My stand and remain”. “I will come in”: the Greek has “and I will come in” (καί introducing the consequence, in the Hebrew manner). “Dine”: Gr. δειπνέω; cf. δεῖπνον, the wedding supper (19:9).

verses.text: The one who conquers, I will grant him to sit with Me on My throne, as I also conquered and sat down with My Father on His throne.
verses.note: “Grant”: Gr. δώσω, lit. “I will give”. Cf. 2:26–27; 22:1.

verses.text: Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

segments.text: And to the angel of the church in Sardis write:
Thus says He who has the Seven Spirits of God
and the seven stars:
I know your works, that you have a name of being alive, and you are dead.
Be watchful, and strengthen the things that remain, which were about to die; for I have not found your works complete before My God.
Remember, then, how you have received and heard, and keep it, and repent. If, then, you do not watch, I will come like a thief, and you will by no means know at what hour I will come upon you.
But you have a few names in Sardis who have not defiled their garments, and they will walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.
The one who conquers will thus be clothed in white garments, and I will by no means blot out his name from the book of life, and I will confess his name before My Father and before His angels.
Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write:
Thus says the Holy One, the True One,
He who has the key of David,
who opens, and no one will shut,
and shuts, and no one opens:
I know your works (behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one is able to shut), that you have little power, and you have kept My word, and have not denied My name.
Behold, I am handing over some of the synagogue of Satan, of those who say they are Jews, and are not, but lie; behold, I will make them come and bow down before your feet, and know that I loved you.
Because you have kept the word of My perseverance, I also will keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole world, to test those who dwell on the earth.
I am coming soon; hold fast what you have, so that no one takes your crown.

The one who conquers, I will make him a pillar in the sanctuary of My God, and he will by no means go out of it again; and I will write on him the name of My God, and the name of the city of My God, the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God, and My new name.
Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
And to the angel of the church in Laodicea write:
Thus says the Amen,
the faithful and true Witness,
the Beginning of the creation of God:
I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot. Would that you were cold or hot!
So, because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I am about to vomit you out of My mouth.
Because you say: I am rich, and have grown rich, and have need of nothing; and you do not know that it is you who are wretched, and pitiable, and poor, and blind, and naked,

I counsel you to buy from Me gold refined by fire, so that you may be rich; and white garments, so that you may clothe yourself and the shame of your nakedness may not be made manifest; and eye salve to anoint your eyes, so that you may see.
As for Me, all whom I love I rebuke and discipline; be zealous, then, and repent.
Behold, I stand at the door and knock; if anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and dine with him, and he with Me.
The one who conquers, I will grant him to sit with Me on My throne, as I also conquered and sat down with My Father on His throne.
Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

verses.text: After these things I saw, and behold, an open door in heaven, and the first voice that I heard, like a trumpet speaking with me, said: Come up here, and I will show you the things that must happen after these things.
verses.note: “After these things”: Gr. μετὰ ταῦτα, as in 1:19; “the things that must happen” takes up 1:1. The SBLGNT punctuates the second “after these things” as the start of 4:2 (“After these things, immediately I was in the Spirit”); the punctuation followed here is that of the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus (without their “and” at the start of 4:2). “Like a trumpet”: cf. 1:10; Ex 19:16–20.

verses.text: Immediately I was in the Spirit; and behold, a throne was set in heaven, and on the throne One seated;
verses.note: “I was”: Gr. ἐγενόμην, as in 1:10. “One seated”: cf. 1 Kgs 22:19; Isa 6:1; Ezek 1:26; Dan 7:9.

verses.text: and He who was seated was like a jasper stone and a sardius in appearance; and around the throne there was a rainbow like an emerald in appearance.
verses.note: “Jasper… sardius”: Gr. ἴασπις and σάρδιον, stones of uncertain identification (cf. 21:11, 19–20). “Rainbow”: cf. Gen 9:13; Ezek 1:28. Variant: the Byzantine text omits “and He who was seated”.

verses.text: Around the throne were twenty-four thrones, and on the thrones twenty-four elders seated, clothed in white garments, and on their heads golden crowns.
verses.note: “Elders”: Gr. πρεσβύτεροι. “Clothed”: Gr. περιβάλλω, lit. “to throw around”, as in 3:5. “Crowns”: Gr. στέφανος (cf. 2:10).

verses.text: From the throne come flashes of lightning, and voices, and thunders; and seven torches of fire burn before the throne, which are the Seven Spirits of God;
verses.note: “Voices”: Gr. φωναί, also “rumblings” (cf. Ex 19:16, Heb. קֹלֹת‎; Rev 8:5; 11:19; 16:18). “Torches”: Gr. λαμπάδες (cf. 8:10; Ezek 1:13; cf. the seven lamps of Zech 4:2). “Seven Spirits”: cf. 1:4.

verses.text: and before the throne, something like a sea of glass, like crystal. In the midst of the throne and around the throne were four living creatures, full of eyes in front and behind.
verses.note: “Sea of glass”: cf. 15:2; Ezek 1:22. “Living creatures”: Gr. ζῷα, lit. “living beings”; cf. Ezek 1:5, Heb. חַיּוֹת‎.

verses.text: The first living creature was like a lion; and the second living creature like a young bull; and the third living creature had a face like that of a man; and the fourth living creature was like a flying eagle.
verses.note: Cf. Ezek 1:10. “Young bull”: Gr. μόσχος.

verses.text: The four living creatures, each of them with six wings, are full of eyes all around and within; and they have no rest, day and night, saying: Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God, the Almighty, He Who Was, and Who Is, and Who Is Coming.
verses.note: Cf. Isa 6:2–3. “He Who Was, and Who Is, and Who Is Coming”: the formula of 1:4, 8, here with “Was” first. “They have no rest, day and night”: the same expression as in 14:11.

verses.text: Whenever the living creatures give glory, and honor, and thanksgiving to Him who is seated on the throne, to Him who lives forever and ever,
verses.note: “Whenever… give”: Gr. ὅταν with the future, a repeated action. “Him who lives forever and ever”: cf. 1:18; 10:6; 15:7; Dan 4:34 (Aram. 4:31); 12:7.

verses.text: the twenty-four elders will fall down before Him who is seated on the throne, and will worship Him who lives forever and ever, and will cast their crowns before the throne, saying:
verses.note: “Will fall down”: Gr. πίπτω, lit. “fall”; before God, prostration in worship (cf. 1:17). “Will worship”: Gr. προσκυνέω, “worship” because the object is God (contrast 3:9, “bow down”). “Will cast”: Gr. βάλλω.

verses.text: Worthy are You, our Lord and God, to receive the glory, and the honor, and the power, for You created all things, and because of Your will they existed and were created.
verses.note: “Created”: Gr. κτίζω (cf. “creation”, 3:14). “Because of Your will”: Gr. διὰ τὸ θέλημά σου. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “Worthy are You, O Lord” (without “and our God”) and “they are and were created”; the Byzantine text adds “the Holy One” after “our Lord and God”.

segments.text: After these things I saw, and behold, an open door in heaven, and the first voice that I heard, like a trumpet speaking with me, said: Come up here, and I will show you the things that must happen after these things.
Immediately I was in the Spirit; and behold, a throne was set in heaven, and on the throne One seated;
and He who was seated was like a jasper stone and a sardius in appearance; and around the throne there was a rainbow like an emerald in appearance.
Around the throne were twenty-four thrones, and on the thrones twenty-four elders seated, clothed in white garments, and on their heads golden crowns.
From the throne come flashes of lightning, and voices, and thunders; and seven torches of fire burn before the throne, which are the Seven Spirits of God;
and before the throne, something like a sea of glass, like crystal. In the midst of the throne and around the throne were four living creatures, full of eyes in front and behind.

The first living creature was like a lion; and the second living creature like a young bull; and the third living creature had a face like that of a man; and the fourth living creature was like a flying eagle.
The four living creatures, each of them with six wings, are full of eyes all around and within; and they have no rest, day and night, saying:
Holy, holy, holy,
the Lord God, the Almighty,
He Who Was, and Who Is, and Who Is Coming.
Whenever the living creatures give glory, and honor, and thanksgiving to Him who is seated on the throne, to Him who lives forever and ever,
the twenty-four elders will fall down before Him who is seated on the throne, and will worship Him who lives forever and ever, and will cast their crowns before the throne, saying:
Worthy are You, our Lord and God,
to receive the glory, and the honor, and the power,
for You created all things,
and because of Your will they existed and were created.

verses.text: And I saw in the right hand of Him who is seated on the throne a book written inside and on the back, sealed with seven seals.
verses.note: “In the right hand”: Gr. ἐπὶ τὴν δεξιάν, lit. “on the right hand”. “On the back”: Gr. ὄπισθεν, lit. “behind”; cf. Ezek 2:9–10. “Sealed with seven seals”: cf. Isa 29:11; Dan 12:4. Variant: the Byzantine text reads “outside” (ἔξωθεν).

verses.text: And I saw a strong angel proclaiming with a loud voice: Who is worthy to open the book and to break its seals?
verses.note: “Strong”: Gr. ἰσχυρός (cf. ἰσχύς, “strength”, 5:12). “Break”: Gr. λῦσαι, lit. “loose”, the same verb as in 1:5 (“freed”).

verses.text: But no one in heaven, or on the earth, or under the earth was able to open the book or to look at it.
I was weeping greatly, because no one was found worthy to open the book or to look at it.
verses.note: Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “to open and to read the book”.

verses.text: Then one of the elders says to me: Do not weep; behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has conquered, to open the book and its seven seals.
verses.note: “The Lion of the tribe of Judah”: cf. Gen 49:9–10. “The Root of David”: cf. Isa 11:1, 10; Rev 22:16. “Has conquered”: Gr. νικάω (cf. 3:21). Variant: the Byzantine text reads “who opens the book”; the Textus Receptus, “to open the book and to loose its seven seals”.

verses.text: And I saw, in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders, a Lamb standing, as though slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the Seven Spirits of God, sent out into all the earth.
verses.note: “Lamb”: Gr. ἀρνίον, a title of Christ in the book (except 13:11). “Slain”: Gr. σφάζω, to slaughter in sacrifice (cf. Isa 53:7, Septuagint σφαγή; Jer 11:19). “Horns”: a symbol of power (cf. Deut 33:17; Ps 89:17). “Seven eyes… sent out into all the earth”: cf. Zech 4:10.

verses.text: He came and took it from the right hand of Him who is seated on the throne.
verses.note: “Took it”: a dramatic perfect (εἴληφεν), rendered as a simple past; the object, the book, is implied. The Textus Receptus makes it explicit (“took the book”).

verses.text: When He had taken the book, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each holding a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.
verses.note: “Fell down”: Gr. πίπτω (cf. 4:10). “Harp”: Gr. κιθάρα, a stringed instrument like the lyre (cf. 14:2; 15:2). “Bowls”: Gr. φιάλαι, the same word as the bowls of wrath (15:7; 16:1). “Prayers of the saints”: cf. Ps 141:2; Rev 8:3–4.

verses.text: They sing a new song, saying: Worthy are You to take the book and to open its seals, for You were slain, and by Your blood You purchased for God those from every tribe, and tongue, and people, and nation;
verses.note: “New song”: cf. Ps 96:1; Isa 42:10; Rev 14:3. “Purchased”: Gr. ἀγοράζω (cf. 14:3–4). “Those from”: the Greek says only “from” (ἐκ), with no expressed object. Variant: Codex Sinaiticus, the Byzantine text, most manuscripts and the Textus Receptus read “purchased us” (ἡμᾶς); the SBLGNT follows Codex Alexandrinus, which omits it. “Tribe, and tongue, and people, and nation”: a formula repeated in the book (cf. 7:9; 14:6).

verses.text: and You made them, for our God, a kingdom and priests; and they will reign on the earth.
verses.note: Cf. 1:6; Ex 19:6. “They will reign”: follows the reading βασιλεύσουσιν, of Codex Sinaiticus and other manuscripts (also in the Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine text and in Nestle 1904); the SBLGNT follows Codex Alexandrinus, which reads βασιλεύουσιν, “they reign”. Cf. 20:4, 6; 22:5. Variant: the Byzantine text reads “kings and priests”; the Textus Receptus, “made us kings and priests… and we will reign”.

verses.text: And I saw, and I heard the voice of many angels around the throne and the living creatures and the elders; and their number was myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands,
verses.note: “Myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands”: cf. Dan 7:10.

verses.text: saying with a loud voice: Worthy is the slain Lamb to receive the power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honor, and glory, and blessing.
verses.note: “Slain Lamb”: a perfect participle (ἐσφαγμένον); the Lamb remains the one who was slain. Seven attributes, governed by a single article in the SBLGNT. “Blessing”: Gr. εὐλογία (cf. 5:13; 7:12).

verses.text: And every creature that is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and on the sea, and all things that are in them, I heard saying: To Him who is seated on the throne and to the Lamb be the blessing, and the honor, and the glory, and the dominion, forever and ever.
verses.note: “Creature”: Gr. κτίσμα (cf. κτίζω, 4:11). “Dominion”: Gr. κράτος (cf. 1:6).

verses.text: The four living creatures were saying: Amen. And the elders fell down and worshiped.
verses.note: Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “the twenty-four elders… and worshiped Him who lives forever and ever”.

segments.text: And I saw in the right hand of Him who is seated on the throne a book written inside and on the back, sealed with seven seals.
And I saw a strong angel proclaiming with a loud voice: Who is worthy to open the book and to break its seals?
But no one in heaven, or on the earth, or under the earth was able to open the book or to look at it.
I was weeping greatly, because no one was found worthy to open the book or to look at it.
Then one of the elders says to me: Do not weep; behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has conquered, to open the book and its seven seals.

And I saw, in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders, a Lamb standing, as though slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the Seven Spirits of God, sent out into all the earth.
He came and took it from the right hand of Him who is seated on the throne.
When He had taken the book, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each holding a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.
They sing a new song, saying:
Worthy are You to take the book
and to open its seals,
for You were slain,
and by Your blood You purchased for God
those from every tribe, and tongue, and people, and nation;
and You made them, for our God,
a kingdom and priests;
and they will reign on the earth.
And I saw, and I heard the voice of many angels around the throne and the living creatures and the elders; and their number was myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands,
saying with a loud voice:
Worthy is the slain Lamb
to receive the power, and riches, and wisdom,
and strength, and honor, and glory, and blessing.
And every creature that is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and on the sea, and all things that are in them, I heard saying:
To Him who is seated on the throne and to the Lamb
be the blessing, and the honor, and the glory, and the dominion,
forever and ever.
The four living creatures were saying: Amen. And the elders fell down and worshiped.

verses.text: And I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying, as with a voice of thunder: Come!
verses.note: “Come”: Gr. ἔρχου. Variant: the Textus Receptus adds “and see” (καὶ βλέπε) in 6:1, 3, 5 and 7; Codex Sinaiticus and the Byzantine text have a similar addition (καὶ ἴδε); in the Byzantine text, in 6:1, 5 and 7.

verses.text: And I saw, and behold, a white horse, and He who sat on it had a bow; a crown was given to Him, and He went out conquering and to conquer.
verses.note: “He who sat”: the capital identifies the rider with the rider of the white horse in 19:11–16; in the book, “white”, “crown” and “conquer” are linked to Christ and His people (cf. 3:21; 5:5; 14:14). Another reading sees here a conquering power. “Bow”: Gr. τόξον. “Crown”: Gr. στέφανος, the victor’s crown (cf. 2:10; 3:11). “Conquering and to conquer”: Gr. νικῶν καὶ ἵνα νικήσῃ (cf. νικάω, 5:5). Horses of different colors: cf. Zech 1:8; 6:1–8.

verses.text: And when He opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying: Come!
Another horse came out, a red one. It was given to him who sat on it to take peace from the earth, and that people should slay one another; and a great sword was given to him.
verses.note: “Red”: Gr. πυρρός, lit. “fire-colored”. “Slay”: Gr. σφάζω, the same verb rendered “slain” in 5:6, 9, 12 and 6:9. “Sword”: Gr. μάχαιρα.

verses.text: And when He opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying: Come! And I saw, and behold, a black horse, and he who sat on it had a balance in his hand.
verses.note: “Balance”: Gr. ζυγός, lit. “yoke”, the beam of the scales.

verses.text: And I heard something like a voice in the midst of the four living creatures, saying: A measure of wheat for a denarius, and three measures of barley for a denarius; and do not harm the oil and the wine.
verses.note: “Measure”: Gr. χοῖνιξ, a little more than a liter (about a quart). “Denarius”: a Roman silver coin (cf. Matt 20:2). “Do not harm”: Gr. ἀδικέω (cf. 2:11; 7:2–3; 9:4). Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “a voice”, without “something like”.

verses.text: And when He opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying: Come!

And I saw, and behold, a pale horse, and he who sat on it had the name Death, and the grave was following him. Authority was given to them over a fourth of the earth, to kill with sword, and with famine, and with pestilence, and by the wild beasts of the earth.
verses.note: “Pale”: Gr. χλωρός, lit. “pale green” (cf. 8:7; 9:4, “green”). “The grave”: Gr. ᾅδης (cf. 1:18). “Sword”: here Gr. ῥομφαία (cf. 1:16). “Pestilence”: Gr. θάνατος, lit. “death”; the Septuagint uses the same word for “pestilence” in Ezek 14:21. Sword, famine, pestilence and wild beasts: cf. Ezek 14:21; Lev 26:22–26. Variant: the Byzantine text reads “was given to him” (singular); the Textus Receptus, like the SBLGNT, has the plural.

verses.text: And when He opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been slain because of the Word of God and because of the testimony that they held.
verses.note: “Altar”: Gr. θυσιαστήριον. “Souls”: Gr. ψυχαί, also “lives” (cf. Lev 4:7; 17:11). “Slain”: Gr. σφάζω (cf. 5:6). “Word of God… testimony”: cf. 1:2, 9. Variant: the Byzantine text reads “the testimony of the Lamb”.

verses.text: They cried out with a loud voice, saying: How long, O Sovereign, the Holy and True One, do You not judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?
verses.note: “Sovereign”: Gr. δεσπότης, “master, owner” (cf. Luke 2:29; Acts 4:24). “The Holy and True One”: cf. 3:7. “How long”: cf. Ps 79:5, 10; Zech 1:12. “Avenge… on”: Gr. ἐκδικέω… ἐκ, lit. “avenge… from” (cf. 19:2; Deut 32:43). “Those who dwell on the earth”: cf. 3:10.

verses.text: Then a white robe was given to each of them, and they were told to rest a little while longer, until the number of their fellow servants and of their brothers, who were about to be killed as they also had been, was completed.
verses.note: “Robe”: Gr. στολή, a long robe (cf. 7:9, 13–14; 22:14). “The number”: the Greek says only “until both their fellow servants and their brothers… were completed”. Variant: the Byzantine text reads “until they complete [their course]” (πληρώσωσιν). “Fellow servants”: Gr. σύνδουλοι (cf. 19:10; 22:9). Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “white robes were given to each”.

verses.text: And I saw when He opened the sixth seal, and there was a great earthquake, and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the whole moon became like blood,
verses.note: “Earthquake”: Gr. σεισμός (cf. 8:5; 11:13, 19; 16:18). “Sackcloth of hair”: Gr. σάκκος τρίχινος, a dark cloth of hair, usually goat’s hair. Sun, moon and stars: cf. Joel 2:10, 31 (Heb. 3:4); Isa 13:10; Matt 24:29. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “and behold, there was” and omits “whole”.

verses.text: and the stars of heaven fell to the earth, as a fig tree casts its unripe figs when it is shaken by a great wind,
verses.note: “Casts”: Gr. βάλλω. “Unripe figs”: Gr. ὄλυνθοι, figs that fall before ripening. Cf. Isa 34:4.

verses.text: and heaven withdrew like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island were moved from their places.
verses.note: “Scroll”: Gr. βιβλίον, “book”, here the scroll that is rolled up (cf. 5:1; Isa 34:4). “Were moved”: plural in the Greek.

verses.text: The kings of the earth, and the great ones, and the commanders, and the rich, and the mighty, and every slave and free man hid themselves in the caves and among the rocks of the mountains;
verses.note: “The great ones”: Gr. μεγιστᾶνες, the nobles. “Commanders”: Gr. χιλίαρχοι, lit. “commanders of a thousand”. “Slave”: Gr. δοῦλος, rendered “servant” in 1:1; here in contrast with “free” (cf. 13:16; 19:18). Cf. Isa 2:10, 19, 21.

verses.text: and they say to the mountains and to the rocks: Fall on us and hide us from the face of Him who is seated on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb,
verses.note: Cf. Hos 10:8; Luke 23:30. “Face”: Gr. πρόσωπον.

verses.text: for the great day of Their wrath has come, and who is able to stand?
verses.note: “Their”: of Him who is seated on the throne and of the Lamb (6:16). Variant: Codex Alexandrinus, the Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “of His wrath”; the SBLGNT is followed, with Codex Sinaiticus and Ephraemi. “Stand”: Gr. σταθῆναι (cf. 5:6, the Lamb “standing”; Nah 1:6; Mal 3:2). “The great day”: cf. Joel 2:11; Zeph 1:14.

segments.text: And I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying, as with a voice of thunder: Come!
And I saw, and behold, a white horse, and He who sat on it had a bow; a crown was given to Him, and He went out conquering and to conquer.
And when He opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying: Come!
Another horse came out, a red one. It was given to him who sat on it to take peace from the earth, and that people should slay one another; and a great sword was given to him.
And when He opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying: Come! And I saw, and behold, a black horse, and he who sat on it had a balance in his hand.

And I heard something like a voice in the midst of the four living creatures, saying: A measure of wheat for a denarius, and three measures of barley for a denarius; and do not harm the oil and the wine.
And when He opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying: Come!

And I saw, and behold, a pale horse, and he who sat on it had the name Death, and the grave was following him. Authority was given to them over a fourth of the earth, to kill with sword, and with famine, and with pestilence, and by the wild beasts of the earth.
And when He opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been slain because of the Word of God and because of the testimony that they held.
They cried out with a loud voice, saying: How long, O Sovereign, the Holy and True One, do You not judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?

Then a white robe was given to each of them, and they were told to rest a little while longer, until the number of their fellow servants and of their brothers, who were about to be killed as they also had been, was completed.
And I saw when He opened the sixth seal, and there was a great earthquake, and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the whole moon became like blood,
and the stars of heaven fell to the earth, as a fig tree casts its unripe figs when it is shaken by a great wind,
and heaven withdrew like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island were moved from their places.
The kings of the earth, and the great ones, and the commanders, and the rich, and the mighty, and every slave and free man hid themselves in the caves and among the rocks of the mountains;
and they say to the mountains and to the rocks: Fall on us and hide us from the face of Him who is seated on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb,
for the great day of Their wrath has come, and who is able to stand?

verses.text: After this I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, so that no wind would blow on the earth, or on the sea, or on any tree.
verses.note: “After this”: Gr. μετὰ τοῦτο (singular); in 7:9, μετὰ ταῦτα, “after these things” (cf. 4:1). Variant: the Byzantine text reads “And after this”; the Textus Receptus, “And after these things”. “Holding”: Gr. κρατέω (cf. 2:1). “Four corners… four winds”: cf. Isa 11:12; Jer 49:36; Dan 7:2; Zech 6:5.

verses.text: And I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the sun, having the seal of the living God; and he cried out with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it was given to harm the earth and the sea,
verses.note: “From the rising of the sun”: that is, from the east. “The seal of the living God”: Gr. σφραγῖδα θεοῦ ζῶντος, lit. “a seal of the living God”. “Harm”: Gr. ἀδικέω (cf. 6:6).

verses.text: saying: Do not harm the earth, or the sea, or the trees, until we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads.
verses.note: “Sealed”: Gr. σφραγίζω (cf. 10:4; 22:10). “Foreheads”: cf. 9:4; 14:1; 22:4; Ezek 9:4; Ex 28:36–38.

verses.text: And I heard the number of those who were sealed: one hundred and forty-four thousand sealed, from every tribe of the sons of Israel:
from the tribe of Judah, twelve thousand sealed; from the tribe of Reuben, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Gad, twelve thousand;
verses.note: The list begins with Judah (cf. 5:5), includes Levi and Joseph, and does not include Dan or Ephraim (cf. Gen 49; Ezek 48). Variant: the Textus Receptus repeats “sealed” after each tribe.

verses.text: from the tribe of Asher, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Naphtali, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Manasseh, twelve thousand;
from the tribe of Simeon, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Levi, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Issachar, twelve thousand;
from the tribe of Zebulun, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Joseph, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Benjamin, twelve thousand sealed.

After these things I saw, and behold, a great multitude that no one could count, from every nation, and tribes, and peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, and with palm branches in their hands;
verses.note: “From every nation, and tribes, and peoples, and tongues”: the order and number of the Greek, with a single preposition (cf. 5:9). “Clothed”: Gr. περιβάλλω (cf. 3:5). “Robes”: Gr. στολαί (cf. 6:11). “Palm branches”: Gr. φοίνικες (cf. Lev 23:40; John 12:13).

verses.text: and they cry out with a loud voice, saying: Salvation to our God, who is seated on the throne, and to the Lamb.
verses.note: “Salvation to our God”: the Greek has no verb (cf. 5:13; 19:1). Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “crying out”.

verses.text: All the angels were standing around the throne and around the elders and the four living creatures, and they fell down on their faces before the throne and worshiped God,
verses.note: “Were standing”: Gr. ἵστημι (cf. 5:6; 6:17). “Fell down”: Gr. πίπτω (cf. 4:10; 5:14).

verses.text: saying: Amen. The blessing, and the glory, and the wisdom, and the thanksgiving, and the honor, and the power, and the strength be to our God forever and ever. Amen.
verses.note: Seven attributes, each with the article (in 5:12, a single article for all seven). “Thanksgiving”: Gr. εὐχαριστία (cf. 4:9).

verses.text: Then one of the elders spoke up, saying to me: These who are clothed in the white robes, who are they, and where did they come from?
verses.note: “Spoke up”: Gr. ἀπεκρίθη, lit. “answered”, with no previous question.

verses.text: I said to him: My lord, you know. And he said to me: These are the ones who came out of the great tribulation, and they washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
verses.note: “Said”: Gr. εἴρηκα, perfect. “My lord”: addressed to the elder; the Textus Receptus omits “my”. “Came out”: Gr. οἱ ἐρχόμενοι, present participle, lit. “those who are coming”; rendered in the past, in harmony with “washed… made white”. “The great tribulation”: Gr. θλῖψις (cf. 1:9; 2:22; Dan 12:1; Matt 24:21). “Washed… made white”: cf. 22:14; Gen 49:11; Isa 1:18; Dan 11:35; 12:10 (Heb.).

verses.text: Therefore they are before the throne of God and serve Him day and night in His sanctuary; and He who is seated on the throne will spread His tabernacle over them.
verses.note: “Serve”: Gr. λατρεύω, the service of worship. “Sanctuary”: Gr. ναός (cf. 3:12; 11:19). “Will spread His tabernacle”: Gr. σκηνόω, “to dwell in a tent” (cf. 13:6; 21:3; John 1:14; Ezek 37:27).

verses.text: They will hunger no more, nor thirst any more, nor will the sun by any means fall on them, nor any scorching heat,
verses.note: Cf. Isa 49:10. “By any means”: Gr. οὐδὲ μή.

verses.text: for the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne will shepherd them and will guide them to springs of the waters of life; and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.
verses.note: “Will shepherd”: Gr. ποιμαίνω (cf. 2:27; Ps 23:1–2; Ezek 34:23). “To springs of the waters of life”: lit. “to springs of waters of life” (cf. Isa 49:10). Variants: the Byzantine text reads “shepherds… guides” (present); the Textus Receptus reads “to living springs of waters”. “Wipe away”: Gr. ἐξαλείφω (cf. 3:5; 21:4; Isa 25:8).

segments.text: After this I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, so that no wind would blow on the earth, or on the sea, or on any tree.

And I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the sun, having the seal of the living God; and he cried out with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it was given to harm the earth and the sea,
saying: Do not harm the earth, or the sea, or the trees, until we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads.
And I heard the number of those who were sealed: one hundred and forty-four thousand sealed, from every tribe of the sons of Israel:
from the tribe of Judah, twelve thousand sealed; from the tribe of Reuben, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Gad, twelve thousand;
from the tribe of Asher, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Naphtali, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Manasseh, twelve thousand;
from the tribe of Simeon, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Levi, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Issachar, twelve thousand;
from the tribe of Zebulun, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Joseph, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Benjamin, twelve thousand sealed.

After these things I saw, and behold, a great multitude that no one could count, from every nation, and tribes, and peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, and with palm branches in their hands;
and they cry out with a loud voice, saying:
Salvation to our God, who is seated on the throne,
and to the Lamb.
All the angels were standing around the throne and around the elders and the four living creatures, and they fell down on their faces before the throne and worshiped God,
saying:
Amen. The blessing, and the glory, and the wisdom,
and the thanksgiving, and the honor, and the power, and the strength
be to our God forever and ever. Amen.
Then one of the elders spoke up, saying to me: These who are clothed in the white robes, who are they, and where did they come from?
I said to him: My lord, you know. And he said to me:
These are the ones who came out of the great tribulation,
and they washed their robes
and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
Therefore they are before the throne of God
and serve Him day and night in His sanctuary;
and He who is seated on the throne
will spread His tabernacle over them.
They will hunger no more, nor thirst any more,
nor will the sun by any means fall on them,
nor any scorching heat,
for the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne will shepherd them
and will guide them to springs of the waters of life;
and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.

verses.text: And when He opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.
verses.note: Cf. Hab 2:20; Zeph 1:7; Zech 2:13 (Heb. 2:17).

verses.text: And I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and seven trumpets were given to them.
verses.note: “Stand”: Gr. ἑστήκασιν, perfect. “Trumpets”: Gr. σάλπιγγες (cf. 1:10; 4:1; Num 10:9; Josh 6:4; Joel 2:1).

verses.text: Then another angel came and stood at the altar, having a golden censer. Much incense was given to him, so that he might add it to the prayers of all the saints on the golden altar that is before the throne.
verses.note: “At the altar”: Gr. ἐπὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, lit. “upon the altar”. “Censer”: Gr. λιβανωτός. “That he might add it to the prayers”: lit. “that he might give it to the prayers”. “Golden altar… before the throne”: cf. Ex 30:1–10; 40:5; Lev 16:12–13.

verses.text: From the hand of the angel, the smoke of the incense went up before God with the prayers of the saints.
verses.note: “With the prayers”: Gr. ταῖς προσευχαῖς, the same dative as in 8:3, rendered there “to the prayers” (cf. 5:8; Ps 141:2).

verses.text: Then the angel took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and cast it onto the earth; and there were thunders, and voices, and flashes of lightning, and an earthquake.
verses.note: “Took”: Gr. εἴληφεν, perfect (cf. 5:7). Cf. Lev 16:12; Ezek 10:2. “Thunders, and voices, and flashes of lightning”: cf. 4:5; 11:19; 16:18; Ex 19:16.

verses.text: The seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to blow their trumpets.
verses.note: “Blow their trumpets”: Gr. σαλπίζω, “to sound the trumpet”.

verses.text: And the first blew his trumpet: there came hail and fire mixed with blood, and they were cast upon the earth. And a third of the earth was burned up, and a third of the trees were burned up, and all green grass was burned up.
verses.note: “Hail and fire”: cf. Ex 9:23–25. “They were cast”: Gr. ἐβλήθη, singular. “Green”: Gr. χλωρός, the same term rendered “pale” in 6:8. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “the first angel” and omits “and a third of the earth was burned up”.

verses.text: And the second angel blew his trumpet: something like a great mountain burning with fire was cast into the sea, and a third of the sea became blood,
verses.note: “Something like a great mountain”: Gr. ὡς ὄρος μέγα. Cf. Jer 51:25. “Became blood”: cf. Ex 7:20–21. Variant: the Byzantine text omits “with fire”; the Textus Receptus has it.

verses.text: and a third of the creatures that were in the sea, those that had life, died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.
verses.note: “Creatures”: Gr. κτίσματα (cf. 5:13). “That had life”: Gr. τὰ ἔχοντα ψυχάς, lit. “that had souls” (cf. 6:9; 16:3).

verses.text: And the third angel blew his trumpet: a great star fell from heaven, burning like a torch, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of the waters.
verses.note: “Torch”: Gr. λαμπάς (cf. 4:5).

verses.text: The star is called Wormwood. A third of the waters became wormwood, and many people died from the waters, because they were made bitter.
verses.note: “The star is called Wormwood”: lit. “the name of the star is called: the Wormwood”. “Wormwood”: Gr. ἄψινθος, a bitter-tasting plant. Cf. Jer 9:15 (Heb. 9:14); 23:15; Amos 5:7; Ex 15:23.

verses.text: And the fourth angel blew his trumpet: a third of the sun was struck, and a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, so that a third of them would be darkened, and the day would not shine for a third of it, and likewise the night.
verses.note: “Was struck”: Gr. πλήσσω. Cf. Ex 10:21–23; Joel 2:10; Amos 8:9.

verses.text: And I saw, and I heard an angel flying in midheaven, saying with a loud voice: Woe, woe, woe to those who dwell on the earth, because of the remaining voices of the trumpet of the three angels who are about to blow!
verses.note: “Angel”: follows the Textus Receptus and some manuscripts (ἀγγέλου; cf. 14:6, another angel “flying in midheaven”); the SBLGNT, codices Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus, and the Byzantine text read “eagle” (ἀετοῦ). “Midheaven”: Gr. μεσουράνημα, the highest point of the sky (cf. 14:6; 19:17). “Woe”: Gr. οὐαί (cf. 9:12; 11:14; 12:12). “Remaining”: Gr. λοιπαί.

segments.text: And when He opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.
And I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and seven trumpets were given to them.

Then another angel came and stood at the altar, having a golden censer. Much incense was given to him, so that he might add it to the prayers of all the saints on the golden altar that is before the throne.
From the hand of the angel, the smoke of the incense went up before God with the prayers of the saints.
Then the angel took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and cast it onto the earth; and there were thunders, and voices, and flashes of lightning, and an earthquake.
The seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to blow their trumpets.

And the first blew his trumpet: there came hail and fire mixed with blood, and they were cast upon the earth. And a third of the earth was burned up, and a third of the trees were burned up, and all green grass was burned up.
And the second angel blew his trumpet: something like a great mountain burning with fire was cast into the sea, and a third of the sea became blood,
and a third of the creatures that were in the sea, those that had life, died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.
And the third angel blew his trumpet: a great star fell from heaven, burning like a torch, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of the waters.
The star is called Wormwood. A third of the waters became wormwood, and many people died from the waters, because they were made bitter.

And the fourth angel blew his trumpet: a third of the sun was struck, and a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, so that a third of them would be darkened, and the day would not shine for a third of it, and likewise the night.

And I saw, and I heard an angel flying in midheaven, saying with a loud voice: Woe, woe, woe to those who dwell on the earth, because of the remaining voices of the trumpet of the three angels who are about to blow!

verses.text: And the fifth angel blew his trumpet: I saw a star that had fallen from heaven to the earth, and the key to the shaft of the abyss was given to him.
verses.note: “That had fallen”: Gr. πεπτωκότα, perfect participle. “Shaft of the abyss”: Gr. φρέαρ τῆς ἀβύσσου (cf. 11:7; 17:8; 20:1–3).

verses.text: He opened the shaft of the abyss, and smoke went up from the shaft like the smoke of a great furnace, and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke of the shaft.
verses.note: “Furnace”: cf. Gen 19:28; Ex 19:18. “Were darkened”: cf. Joel 2:10. Variant: the Byzantine text reads “a burning furnace”.

verses.text: From the smoke came locusts upon the earth, and authority was given to them, as the scorpions of the earth have authority.
They were told not to harm the grass of the earth, or any green thing, or any tree, except the people who do not have the seal of God on the foreheads.
verses.note: “Green thing”: Gr. χλωρόν, lit. “green” (cf. 8:7). “Except”: Gr. εἰ μή. “The seal of God on the foreheads”: cf. 7:2–3; Ezek 9:4, 6. Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “on their foreheads”; the Textus Receptus also reads “only the people”.

verses.text: And it was given to them not to kill them, but that they should be tormented for five months; and their torment was like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a person.
verses.note: “Tormented”: Gr. βασανίζω (cf. 14:10; 20:10). “Five months”: cf. 9:10. “Strikes”: Gr. παίω, “to hit”.

verses.text: In those days people will seek death and will by no means find it; and they will long to die, and death flees from them.
verses.note: “By no means”: Gr. οὐ μή; the Textus Receptus reads “will not find”. “Flees”: present in the Greek; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “will flee”. Cf. Job 3:21; Jer 8:3.

verses.text: The forms of the locusts were like horses prepared for war; and on their heads were something like crowns resembling gold, and their faces were like the faces of men,
verses.note: “Forms”: Gr. ὁμοιώματα, lit. “likenesses”. “Horses prepared for war”: cf. Joel 2:4–5; Job 39:19–25. “Something like crowns”: Gr. ὡς στέφανοι.

verses.text: and they had hair like the hair of women, and their teeth were like those of lions,
verses.note: “Teeth… of lions”: cf. Joel 1:6.

verses.text: and they had breastplates like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the sound of chariots of many horses running to war.
verses.note: “Sound”: Gr. φωνή, “voice”. Cf. Joel 2:5.

verses.text: They have tails like scorpions, and stings; and in their tails is their authority to harm people for five months.
verses.note: “Stings”: Gr. κέντρα. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “and there were stings in their tails”; the Byzantine text, “and they have authority to harm”.

verses.text: They have over them as king the angel of the abyss; his name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek he has the name Apollyon.
verses.note: “Abaddon”: Heb. אֲבַדּוֹן‎, “destruction” (cf. Job 26:6; 28:22; Ps 88:11 (Heb. 88:12); Prov 15:11). “Apollyon”: Gr. Ἀπολλύων, “destroyer”.

verses.text: The first woe has passed; behold, two woes are still coming after these things.
And the sixth angel blew his trumpet: I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar that is before God,
verses.note: “A voice”: Gr. φωνὴν μίαν, lit. “a single voice”. “Horns of the golden altar”: cf. Ex 30:1–3; Rev 8:3. “Four”: Gr. τεσσάρων, following the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus; the SBLGNT follows Papyrus 47 and Codex Alexandrinus, which omit “four”.

verses.text: saying to the sixth angel, who had the trumpet: Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates.
verses.note: “Release”: Gr. λῦσον. “Bound”: Gr. δεδεμένους, perfect participle. “The great river Euphrates”: cf. 16:12; Gen 15:18; Isa 8:7.

verses.text: Then the four angels were released, who had been prepared for the hour, and day, and month, and year, to kill a third of mankind.
verses.note: “For the hour, and day, and month, and year”: a single article for the four terms, which may indicate an appointed moment. Alternative reading: a period formed by adding the four terms together (cf. Num 14:34; Ezek 4:6, a day for a year). Variant: the Byzantine text reads “for the hour and for the day”.

verses.text: The number of the armies of the cavalry was two hundred million; I heard their number.
verses.note: “Two hundred million”: Gr. δισμυριάδες μυριάδων, lit. “two myriads of myriads”, that is, twice ten thousand times ten thousand (cf. 5:11; Dan 7:10). Variant: the Byzantine text reads “myriads of myriads”.

verses.text: Thus I saw the horses in the vision, and those who sat on them, having breastplates the color of fire, and of jacinth, and of sulfur; and the heads of the horses were like the heads of lions, and out of their mouths come fire, and smoke, and sulfur.
verses.note: “The color of fire… of jacinth… of sulfur”: Gr. πυρίνους, ὑακινθίνους, θειώδεις, lit. “of fire, of jacinth, of sulfur”; jacinth is a dark-blue or purple stone. “Fire, and smoke, and sulfur”: cf. Gen 19:24, 28; Rev 14:10; 19:20; 21:8.

verses.text: By these three plagues a third of mankind was killed: by the fire, and by the smoke, and by the sulfur that came out of their mouths.
verses.note: “Plagues”: Gr. πληγαί (cf. 15:1; 16:9). Variant: the Textus Receptus omits “plagues”.

verses.text: For the authority of the horses is in their mouth and in their tails; for their tails are like serpents, having heads, and with them they do harm.
verses.note: Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “their authority” in place of “the authority of the horses”.

verses.text: The rest of mankind, who were not killed by these plagues, even so did not repent of the works of their hands, so as not to worship the demons and the idols of gold, and of silver, and of bronze, and of stone, and of wood, which can neither see, nor hear, nor walk;
verses.note: “Even so did not”: Gr. οὐδέ; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “did not”. “The rest”: Gr. λοιποί (cf. 19:21; 20:5). “So as not to worship”: Gr. ἵνα μή. “Idols… which can neither see”: cf. Deut 4:28; Ps 115:4–7; 135:15–17; Dan 5:23.

verses.text: and they did not repent of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their prostitution, nor of their thefts.
verses.note: “Sorceries”: Gr. φάρμακα, lit. “drugs, potions”, here in the sense of spells; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read φαρμακειῶν, “sorceries”. “Prostitution”: Gr. πορνεία (cf. 2:21).

segments.text: And the fifth angel blew his trumpet: I saw a star that had fallen from heaven to the earth, and the key to the shaft of the abyss was given to him.
He opened the shaft of the abyss, and smoke went up from the shaft like the smoke of a great furnace, and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke of the shaft.
From the smoke came locusts upon the earth, and authority was given to them, as the scorpions of the earth have authority.
They were told not to harm the grass of the earth, or any green thing, or any tree, except the people who do not have the seal of God on the foreheads.
And it was given to them not to kill them, but that they should be tormented for five months; and their torment was like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a person.
In those days people will seek death and will by no means find it; and they will long to die, and death flees from them.
The forms of the locusts were like horses prepared for war; and on their heads were something like crowns resembling gold, and their faces were like the faces of men,
and they had hair like the hair of women, and their teeth were like those of lions,
and they had breastplates like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the sound of chariots of many horses running to war.
They have tails like scorpions, and stings; and in their tails is their authority to harm people for five months.
They have over them as king the angel of the abyss; his name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek he has the name Apollyon.
The first woe has passed; behold, two woes are still coming after these things.
And the sixth angel blew his trumpet: I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar that is before God,
saying to the sixth angel, who had the trumpet: Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates.
Then the four angels were released, who had been prepared for the hour, and day, and month, and year, to kill a third of mankind.
The number of the armies of the cavalry was two hundred million; I heard their number.

Thus I saw the horses in the vision, and those who sat on them, having breastplates the color of fire, and of jacinth, and of sulfur; and the heads of the horses were like the heads of lions, and out of their mouths come fire, and smoke, and sulfur.
By these three plagues a third of mankind was killed: by the fire, and by the smoke, and by the sulfur that came out of their mouths.
For the authority of the horses is in their mouth and in their tails; for their tails are like serpents, having heads, and with them they do harm.

The rest of mankind, who were not killed by these plagues, even so did not repent of the works of their hands, so as not to worship the demons and the idols of gold, and of silver, and of bronze, and of stone, and of wood, which can neither see, nor hear, nor walk;
and they did not repent of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their prostitution, nor of their thefts.

headings.text: The angel and the little book

verses.text: And I saw another strong Angel coming down from heaven, clothed in a cloud, and the rainbow on His head, and His face like the sun, and His feet like pillars of fire,
verses.note: “Angel”: the capital identifies this Angel with Christ; the rainbow, the face like the sun and the feet like pillars of fire recall the divine figures of 1:15–16 and 4:3 and the man clothed in linen of Dan 10:5–6; 12:7. Another reading sees here a mighty angel (cf. 5:2; 18:21). “Clothed in a cloud”: Gr. περιβάλλω (cf. 3:5). “The rainbow”: Gr. ἡ ἶρις (cf. 4:3). “His face like the sun”: cf. 1:16. “Pillars of fire”: cf. Ex 13:21. Variant: the Byzantine text omits “another”.

verses.text: and He had in His hand an open little book. He set His right foot on the sea, and His left on the earth,
verses.note: “Little book”: Gr. βιβλαρίδιον, a diminutive of βιβλίον, “book” (cf. 5:1; 10:8); the Byzantine text reads βιβλίον. “Open”: Gr. ἠνεῳγμένον, perfect participle.

verses.text: and He cried out with a loud voice, as a lion roars. When He cried out, the seven thunders uttered their voices.
verses.note: “As a lion roars”: Gr. μυκᾶται, lit. “bellows” (cf. Hos 11:10; Amos 3:8). “Uttered their voices”: lit. “spoke their own voices”. “The seven thunders”: cf. Ps 29:3–9.

verses.text: When the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to write, and I heard a voice from heaven, saying: Seal up what the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write it.
verses.note: “Seal up”: Gr. σφράγισον (cf. Dan 8:26; 12:4, 9; Rev 22:10).

verses.text: Then the Angel whom I saw standing on the sea and on the earth raised His right hand to heaven,
verses.note: “Raised His right hand to heaven”: cf. Dan 12:7; Deut 32:40. Variant: the Textus Receptus omits “right”.

verses.text: and swore by Him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and the things in it, and the earth and the things in it, and the sea and the things in it: There will be no more time;
verses.note: “Him who lives forever and ever”: cf. 4:9–10. “Who created heaven… and the sea”: cf. 14:7; Ex 20:11; Neh 9:6. “There will be no more time”: Gr. ὅτι χρόνος οὐκέτι ἔσται, lit. “that time will be no longer”; alternative reading: “there will be no more delay”.

verses.text: but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to blow his trumpet, the mystery of God will be completed, as He announced the good news to His servants the prophets.
verses.note: “Will be completed”: Gr. καὶ ἐτελέσθη, aorist, lit. “and was completed”, with a future sense (cf. 15:1); the Textus Receptus reads τελεσθῇ, “should be completed”. “Mystery”: Gr. μυστήριον (cf. 1:20; 17:5, 7). “Announced the good news”: Gr. εὐηγγέλισεν (cf. 14:6; Amos 3:7).
