verses.text: The voice that I had heard from heaven spoke with me again, saying: Go, take the open book in the hand of the Angel who is standing on the sea and on the earth.
verses.note: “Book”: here Gr. βιβλίον; the Textus Receptus reads βιβλαρίδιον, and the Byzantine text βιβλιδάριον, both “little book”.

verses.text: I went to the Angel, telling Him to give me the little book. And He says to me: Take it and devour it; it will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet as honey.
verses.note: “Devour it”: Gr. κατάφαγε, an intensive form of “eat”. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “saying to him: Give me the little book”. “Stomach”: Gr. κοιλία. Cf. Ezek 2:8–3:3; Jer 15:16 (Heb.); Ps 119:103.

verses.text: I took the little book from the hand of the Angel and devoured it; in my mouth it was sweet as honey, but when I had eaten it, my stomach became bitter.
verses.note: “Became bitter”: Gr. ἐπικράνθη (cf. 8:11). Variant: the Byzantine text reads βιβλίον, “book”, for “little book”.

verses.text: And they say to me: You must prophesy again about many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings.
verses.note: “They say to me”: plural in the Greek; the Textus Receptus reads “he says to me”. “About”: Gr. ἐπί with the dative, also “before” (in the presence of) or “against”. “Many”: in the Greek it comes after “kings” (βασιλεῦσιν πολλοῖς), but it can apply to all the terms. “Peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings”: cf. 5:9; 7:9; 17:15.

blocks.text: The angel and the little book

segments.text: And I saw another strong Angel coming down from heaven, clothed in a cloud, and the rainbow on His head, and His face like the sun, and His feet like pillars of fire,
and He had in His hand an open little book. He set His right foot on the sea, and His left on the earth,
and He cried out with a loud voice, as a lion roars. When He cried out, the seven thunders uttered their voices.
When the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to write, and I heard a voice from heaven, saying: Seal up what the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write it.
Then the Angel whom I saw standing on the sea and on the earth raised His right hand to heaven,
and swore by Him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and the things in it, and the earth and the things in it, and the sea and the things in it: There will be no more time;
but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to blow his trumpet, the mystery of God will be completed, as He announced the good news to His servants the prophets.
The voice that I had heard from heaven spoke with me again, saying: Go, take the open book in the hand of the Angel who is standing on the sea and on the earth.
I went to the Angel, telling Him to give me the little book. And He says to me: Take it and devour it; it will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet as honey.
I took the little book from the hand of the Angel and devoured it; in my mouth it was sweet as honey, but when I had eaten it, my stomach became bitter.
And they say to me: You must prophesy again about many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings.

verses.text: A reed like a rod was given to me, and I was told: Rise and measure the sanctuary of God, and the altar, and those who worship in it.
verses.note: “Reed”: Gr. κάλαμος, “reed, cane”, used as a measuring rod; Ezekiel’s was six long cubits, about 3 meters (10 feet) (Ezek 40:3–5; cf. 21:15–16). “Like a rod”: Gr. ὅμοιος ῥάβδῳ; ῥάβδος is “rod, staff”, the same word as in 2:27; 12:5; 19:15 (“rod of iron”). “I was told”: Gr. λέγων, lit. “saying”, with no expressed subject; the Textus Receptus reads “and the angel stood, saying”. “Sanctuary”: Gr. ναός (cf. 3:12; 7:15). “Measure”: cf. Ezek 40–42; Zech 2:1–2 (Heb. 2:5–6).

verses.text: And the court that is outside the sanctuary, leave it out, and do not measure it, for it was given to the nations; and they will trample the holy city for forty-two months.
verses.note: “Leave it out”: Gr. ἔκβαλε ἔξωθεν, lit. “cast it outside”. “Trample”: cf. Luke 21:24; Dan 8:13. “Forty-two months”: cf. 11:3; 12:6, 14; 13:5; Dan 7:25; 12:7.

verses.text: And I will grant My two witnesses to prophesy for one thousand two hundred and sixty days, clothed in sackcloth.
verses.note: “I will grant… to prophesy”: lit. “I will give… and they will prophesy” (cf. 3:21). “Witnesses”: Gr. μάρτυσιν (cf. 1:5; 2:13). “One thousand two hundred and sixty days”: cf. 12:6. “Sackcloth”: Gr. σάκκους (cf. 6:12).

verses.text: These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth.
verses.note: “Olive trees… lampstands”: cf. Zech 4:2–3, 11–14; Rev 1:20. “Lord of the earth”: the Textus Receptus reads “God of the earth”.

verses.text: And if anyone wants to harm them, fire comes out of their mouth and devours their enemies; and if anyone would harm them, in this way he must be killed.
verses.note: “Fire… devours their enemies”: cf. 2 Kgs 1:10–12; Jer 5:14.

verses.text: These have authority to shut the sky, so that no rain may fall during the days of their prophecy; and they have authority over the waters to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with every plague, as often as they wish.
verses.note: “Shut the sky… rain”: cf. 1 Kgs 17:1; Jas 5:17. “Waters… into blood”: cf. Ex 7:17–20. “Plague”: Gr. πληγή (cf. 9:18).

verses.text: And when they have completed their testimony, the beast that comes up out of the abyss will make war against them, and conquer them, and kill them.
verses.note: “Completed”: Gr. τελέσωσιν (cf. 10:7). “Beast”: Gr. θηρίον (cf. 13:1; 17:8; Dan 7:3, 7, 21). “Comes up out of the abyss”: cf. 9:1; 17:8.

verses.text: Their dead body will lie in the street of the great city that is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where also their Lord was crucified.
verses.note: “Dead body”: Gr. τὸ πτῶμα, singular, also in 11:9a; plural in 11:9b. Variants: the Textus Receptus reads “dead bodies” (also in 11:9a) and “our Lord”. “Will lie”: the Greek has no verb. “Spiritually”: Gr. πνευματικῶς. “Sodom and Egypt”: cf. Isa 1:9–10; Ezek 16:46–49.

verses.text: Some from the peoples, and tribes, and tongues, and nations look at their dead body for three and a half days, and do not permit their dead bodies to be placed in a tomb.
verses.note: “Some from”: Gr. ἐκ τῶν, lit. “from among” (cf. 5:9). “Peoples, and tribes, and tongues, and nations”: cf. 5:9; 7:9; 10:11. “Tomb”: Gr. μνῆμα.

verses.text: Those who dwell on the earth rejoice over them and are glad, and will send gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented those who dwell on the earth.
verses.note: “Tormented”: Gr. βασανίζω (cf. 9:5). Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “will not permit” (11:9) and “will be glad”; the Textus Receptus also reads “will look” (11:9).

verses.text: After the three and a half days, a breath of life from God entered them, and they stood on their feet, and great fear fell on those who were watching them.
verses.note: “Breath of life”: Gr. πνεῦμα ζωῆς, “spirit, breath of life” (cf. Gen 2:7, Septuagint πνοή; Ezek 37:5, 10); the Septuagint uses πνεῦμα ζωῆς in Gen 7:15 and Ezek 37:5. “Stood on their feet”: cf. Ezek 37:10.

verses.text: Then they heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them: Come up here. And they went up to heaven in the cloud, and their enemies watched them.
verses.note: “Come up here”: cf. 4:1. “In the cloud”: cf. 2 Kgs 2:11; Acts 1:9. Variant: the Byzantine text reads “And I heard”.

verses.text: In that hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell, and seven thousand names of men were killed in the earthquake; and the rest were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.
verses.note: “Seven thousand names of men”: Gr. ὀνόματα ἀνθρώπων, that is, persons (cf. 3:4). Variant: the Byzantine text reads “in that day”. “The rest”: Gr. λοιποί (cf. 9:20). “Gave glory”: cf. 14:7; 16:9.

verses.text: The second woe has passed; behold, the third woe is coming soon.
And the seventh angel blew his trumpet: there were loud voices in heaven, saying: The kingdom of the world has become our Lord’s and His Christ’s, and He will reign forever and ever.
verses.note: “Has become”: Gr. ἐγένετο. “His Christ”: Gr. τοῦ χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ, “His Anointed” (cf. Ps 2:2; Dan 2:44; 7:14, 27). Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “the kingdoms of the world have become”.

verses.text: Then the twenty-four elders who sit before God on their thrones fell down on their faces and worshiped God,
verses.note: “Before God”: the Byzantine text reads “before the throne of God”.

verses.text: saying: We give You thanks, O Lord God, the Almighty, He Who Is, and Who Was, for You have taken Your great power and have begun to reign.
verses.note: “He Who Is, and Who Was”: without “and Who Is Coming” (cf. 1:4, 8; 4:8); the Textus Receptus adds “and Who Is Coming”. “Have taken”: Gr. εἴληφας, perfect. “Have begun to reign”: Gr. ἐβασίλευσας, lit. “You reigned”.

verses.text: And the nations were enraged, and Your wrath has come, and the time for the dead to be judged, and for giving the reward to Your servants the prophets, and to the saints, and to those who fear Your name, the small and the great, and for destroying those who destroy the earth.
verses.note: “The nations were enraged”: cf. Ps 2:1–5; 99:1 [LXX 98:1]. “The time for the dead to be judged”: Gr. ὁ καιρὸς τῶν νεκρῶν κριθῆναι; καιρός = “time” (cf. 1:3; Dan 7:10, 22). “Reward”: Gr. μισθός (cf. 22:12). “The small and the great”: cf. 13:16; 19:5; 20:12; Ps 115:13 [LXX 113:21]. “Destroying those who destroy”: Gr. διαφθεῖραι… διαφθείροντας, also “corrupt”.

verses.text: The sanctuary of God that is in heaven was opened, and the ark of His covenant was seen in His sanctuary; and there were flashes of lightning, and voices, and thunders, and an earthquake, and great hail.
verses.note: “Sanctuary… in heaven”: Gr. ναός (cf. 15:5; Heb 8:1–5; 9:24). “Ark of His covenant”: Gr. κιβωτὸς τῆς διαθήκης (cf. Ex 25:10–22; Deut 10:1–5; Heb 9:4). “Flashes of lightning, and voices, and thunders”: cf. 4:5; 8:5; 16:18. Variant: the Byzantine text reads “the ark of the covenant of the Lord” and omits “and an earthquake”.

segments.text: A reed like a rod was given to me, and I was told: Rise and measure the sanctuary of God, and the altar, and those who worship in it.
And the court that is outside the sanctuary, leave it out, and do not measure it, for it was given to the nations; and they will trample the holy city for forty-two months.
And I will grant My two witnesses to prophesy for one thousand two hundred and sixty days, clothed in sackcloth.
These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth.
And if anyone wants to harm them, fire comes out of their mouth and devours their enemies; and if anyone would harm them, in this way he must be killed.

These have authority to shut the sky, so that no rain may fall during the days of their prophecy; and they have authority over the waters to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with every plague, as often as they wish.
And when they have completed their testimony, the beast that comes up out of the abyss will make war against them, and conquer them, and kill them.
Their dead body will lie in the street of the great city that is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where also their Lord was crucified.
Some from the peoples, and tribes, and tongues, and nations look at their dead body for three and a half days, and do not permit their dead bodies to be placed in a tomb.
Those who dwell on the earth rejoice over them and are glad, and will send gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented those who dwell on the earth.
After the three and a half days, a breath of life from God entered them, and they stood on their feet, and great fear fell on those who were watching them.
Then they heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them: Come up here. And they went up to heaven in the cloud, and their enemies watched them.

In that hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell, and seven thousand names of men were killed in the earthquake; and the rest were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.
The second woe has passed; behold, the third woe is coming soon.
And the seventh angel blew his trumpet: there were loud voices in heaven, saying:
The kingdom of the world has become
our Lord’s and His Christ’s,
and He will reign forever and ever.
Then the twenty-four elders who sit before God on their thrones fell down on their faces and worshiped God,
saying:
We give You thanks, O Lord God, the Almighty,
He Who Is, and Who Was,
for You have taken Your great power
and have begun to reign.
And the nations were enraged,
and Your wrath has come,
and the time for the dead to be judged,
and for giving the reward to Your servants the prophets,
and to the saints, and to those who fear Your name,
the small and the great,
and for destroying those who destroy the earth.

The sanctuary of God that is in heaven was opened, and the ark of His covenant was seen in His sanctuary; and there were flashes of lightning, and voices, and thunders, and an earthquake, and great hail.

verses.text: And a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars;
verses.note: “Sign”: Gr. σημεῖον (cf. 12:3; 15:1). “Clothed with the sun”: Gr. περιβάλλω (cf. 3:5). “Twelve stars”: cf. Gen 37:9. “Crown”: Gr. στέφανος (cf. 2:10).

verses.text: and she is with child; and she cries out, in labor pains and in torment to give birth.
verses.note: “Cries out”: present in the Greek, as in the Textus Receptus; the Byzantine text reads “cried out”. “Labor pains”: Gr. ὠδίνω (cf. Isa 26:17; 66:7–8; Mic 4:10). “In torment”: Gr. βασανίζω (cf. 9:5).

verses.text: And another sign appeared in heaven, and behold, a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and on his heads seven diadems.
verses.note: “Red”: Gr. πυρρός, lit. “fire-colored” (cf. 6:4). “Seven heads and ten horns”: cf. 13:1; 17:3, 7; Dan 7:7, 20, 24. “Diadems”: Gr. διαδήματα (cf. 13:1; 19:12).

verses.text: His tail sweeps away a third of the stars of heaven, and cast them to the earth. The dragon was standing before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she gave birth he might devour her Child.
verses.note: “Sweeps away”: present in the Greek. “A third of the stars”: cf. Dan 8:10. “Was standing”: Gr. ἕστηκεν, perfect. “Devour”: Gr. καταφάγῃ (cf. 10:9). “Child”: Gr. τέκνον; for the capital, cf. 12:5.

verses.text: She gave birth to a Son, a male Child, who is about to shepherd all the nations with a rod of iron; and her Child was caught up to God and to His throne.
verses.note: “A Son, a male Child”: Gr. υἱὸν ἄρσεν (cf. Isa 66:7); the capital follows the identification given in the verse itself, the rod of iron of Ps 2:9. “Is about to”: Gr. μέλλει (cf. 1:19). “Shepherd… with a rod of iron”: cf. 2:27; 19:15; Ps 2:9. “Caught up”: Gr. ἡρπάσθη, “seized, snatched away”.

verses.text: The woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, so that there they may nourish her for one thousand two hundred and sixty days.
verses.note: “Wilderness”: Gr. ἔρημος (cf. 12:14; 17:3). “They may nourish”: Gr. τρέφωσιν, an impersonal plural. “One thousand two hundred and sixty days”: cf. 11:3; 12:14; 13:5.

verses.text: And there was war in heaven: Michael and His angels made war against the dragon. And the dragon and his angels made war,
verses.note: “Michael”: cf. Dan 10:13, 21; 12:1; Jude 9. “His”: the capital identifies Michael with Christ: the “great prince” who stands up over “the sons of your people” (Dan 12:1), the archangel (Jude 9) whose voice accompanies the Lord’s descent (1 Thess 4:16). Another reading sees here a created archangel, distinct from Christ. “Made war”: lit. “Michael and his angels to make war”, an infinitive in the Greek (τοῦ πολεμῆσαι); the Textus Receptus has the finite verb (ἐπολέμησαν).

verses.text: and he did not prevail, nor was a place found for them any longer in heaven.
verses.note: “He did not prevail”: singular in the Greek (the dragon), with Codex Alexandrinus and the Byzantine text; Codex Sinaiticus and the Textus Receptus read the plural, “they did not prevail”. The Byzantine text also reads “for him” in place of “for them”.

verses.text: And the great dragon was cast down, the ancient serpent, who is called the devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world; he was cast down to the earth, and his angels were cast down with him.
verses.note: “The ancient serpent”: cf. 20:2; Gen 3:1, 14. “devil”: Gr. διάβολος, “accuser, slanderer”. “Satan”: Heb. “adversary” (cf. Job 1:6; Zech 3:1). “Deceives”: Gr. πλανάω (cf. 2:20). “The whole world”: cf. 3:10.

verses.text: And I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying: Now have come the salvation, and the power, and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of His Christ, for the accuser of our brothers was cast down, who accuses them before our God day and night.
verses.note: “Now”: Gr. ἄρτι. “His Christ”: cf. 11:15. “Accuser”: Gr. κατήγωρ (cf. Job 1:9–11; Zech 3:1).

verses.text: And they conquered him because of the blood of the Lamb and because of the word of their testimony, and they did not love their life even to death.
verses.note: “Because of”: Gr. διά with the accusative. “Testimony”: Gr. μαρτυρία (cf. 6:9). “Life”: Gr. ψυχή (cf. Mark 8:35; John 12:25).

verses.text: Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and you who have your tabernacle in them. Woe to the earth and the sea, for the devil has come down to you, having great fury, knowing that he has little time.
verses.note: “Rejoice”: Gr. εὐφραίνω (cf. 11:10). “Have your tabernacle”: Gr. σκηνοῦντες, “dwelling in a tent” (cf. 7:15; 13:6), in contrast with “those who dwell on the earth” (κατοικέω). “Woe”: Gr. οὐαί (cf. 8:13). “Fury”: Gr. θυμός (cf. 14:8, 10; 16:19). “Little time”: Gr. ὀλίγον καιρόν. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “Woe to those who dwell on the earth and the sea”.

verses.text: When the dragon saw that he had been cast down to the earth, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male Child.
verses.note: “The male Child”: Gr. τὸν ἄρσενα (cf. 12:5).

verses.text: The two wings of the great eagle were given to the woman, so that she might fly into the wilderness, to her place, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time, away from the face of the serpent.
verses.note: “Great eagle”: cf. Ex 19:4; Deut 32:11; Isa 40:31. “A time, and times, and half a time”: Gr. καιρὸν καὶ καιροὺς καὶ ἥμισυ καιροῦ (cf. 12:6; Dan 7:25; 12:7). “Away from the face”: Gr. ἀπὸ προσώπου. Variant: the Byzantine text reads “so that she may be nourished”.

verses.text: Then the serpent cast water like a river out of his mouth after the woman, so that she would be swept away by the river.
verses.note: “Swept away by the river”: Gr. ποταμοφόρητον. Cf. Ps 18:4 (Heb. 18:5); 124:4; Isa 43:2.

verses.text: But the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river that the dragon had cast out of his mouth.
verses.note: “Swallowed”: cf. Num 16:30–32.

verses.text: Then the dragon was enraged with the woman, and went off to make war against the remnant of her offspring, those who keep the commandments of God and have the Testimony of Jesus. And he stood on the sand of the sea.
verses.note: “Remnant”: Gr. οἱ λοιποί (cf. 2:24). “Offspring”: Gr. σπέρμα, lit. “seed” (cf. Gen 3:15). “Keep the commandments of God”: cf. 14:12. “The Testimony of Jesus”: cf. 1:2, 9; 19:10. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “the Testimony of Jesus Christ”. “And he stood”: the dragon. In the critical editions of the Greek this sentence is v. 18; here the traditional verse count is kept and the sentence is joined to v. 17. The text follows the SBLGNT, with Papyrus 47 and codices Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus. Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “And I stood” and place the sentence at the beginning of 13:1.

segments.text: And a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars;
and she is with child; and she cries out, in labor pains and in torment to give birth.
And another sign appeared in heaven, and behold, a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and on his heads seven diadems.

His tail sweeps away a third of the stars of heaven, and cast them to the earth. The dragon was standing before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she gave birth he might devour her Child.
She gave birth to a Son, a male Child, who is about to shepherd all the nations with a rod of iron; and her Child was caught up to God and to His throne.
The woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, so that there they may nourish her for one thousand two hundred and sixty days.
And there was war in heaven: Michael and His angels made war against the dragon. And the dragon and his angels made war,
and he did not prevail, nor was a place found for them any longer in heaven.
And the great dragon was cast down, the ancient serpent, who is called the devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world; he was cast down to the earth, and his angels were cast down with him.
And I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying:
Now have come the salvation, and the power,
and the kingdom of our God,
and the authority of His Christ,
for the accuser of our brothers was cast down,
who accuses them before our God day and night.
And they conquered him because of the blood of the Lamb
and because of the word of their testimony,
and they did not love their life even to death.
Therefore rejoice, O heavens,
and you who have your tabernacle in them.
Woe to the earth and the sea,
for the devil has come down to you,
having great fury,
knowing that he has little time.
When the dragon saw that he had been cast down to the earth, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male Child.

The two wings of the great eagle were given to the woman, so that she might fly into the wilderness, to her place, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time, away from the face of the serpent.
Then the serpent cast water like a river out of his mouth after the woman, so that she would be swept away by the river.
But the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river that the dragon had cast out of his mouth.

Then the dragon was enraged with the woman, and went off to make war against the remnant of her offspring, those who keep the commandments of God and have the Testimony of Jesus. And he stood on the sand of the sea.

headings.text: The beast that rises from the sea
The beast that rises from the earth

verses.text: And I saw a beast coming up out of the sea, having ten horns and seven heads, and on its horns ten diadems, and on its heads names of blasphemy.
verses.note: “Coming up out of the sea”: cf. Dan 7:3. “Ten horns and seven heads”: cf. 12:3; 17:3, 7, 12; Dan 7:7, 24; the Textus Receptus reverses the order (“seven heads and ten horns”). “Names of blasphemy”: the Textus Receptus reads “name”. Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus begin the verse with “And I stood on the sand of the sea” (cf. 12:17).

verses.text: The beast that I saw was like a leopard, and its feet were like those of a bear, and its mouth like the mouth of a lion. The dragon gave it his power, and his throne, and great authority.
verses.note: “Leopard… bear… lion”: cf. Dan 7:4–6. “Power… throne… authority”: Gr. δύναμις, θρόνος, ἐξουσία (cf. 2:13; 12:9).

verses.text: And one of its heads was as though slain to death, and its mortal wound was healed. And the whole earth marveled, following the beast,
verses.note: “And one of its heads was”: lit. “and one of its heads”, with no verb; the Textus Receptus reads “And I saw one of its heads”. “As though slain to death”: Gr. ὡς ἐσφαγμένην εἰς θάνατον, the same participle used for the Lamb (5:6, “as though slain”, in the neuter). “Mortal wound”: Gr. ἡ πληγὴ τοῦ θανάτου, lit. “the wound of its death”; πληγή, also “plague” (cf. 9:18). “Following the beast”: lit. “after the beast”.

verses.text: and they worshiped the dragon, because he had given his authority to the beast; and they worshiped the beast, saying: Who is like the beast? And who is able to make war against it?
A mouth was given to it, speaking great things and blasphemies, and authority was given to it to act for forty-two months.
verses.note: “Great things and blasphemies”: cf. Dan 7:8, 11, 20, 25. “To act”: Gr. ποιῆσαι, “to do, to act”; alternative reading: “to continue”. Variant: the Byzantine text reads “blasphemy” (singular) and “to make war”. “Forty-two months”: cf. 11:2; 12:6, 14.

verses.text: It opened its mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme His name and His tabernacle, those who have their tabernacle in heaven.
verses.note: “Tabernacle… those who have their tabernacle in heaven”: Gr. σκηνή… σκηνοῦντας (cf. 7:15; 12:12; 21:3); the Textus Receptus reads “and those who”; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “blasphemy”, singular. Cf. Dan 8:10–11; 11:36.

verses.text: And it was granted to make war against the saints and to conquer them; and authority was given to it over every tribe, and people, and tongue, and nation.
verses.note: “Make war against the saints and to conquer them”: cf. 11:7; Dan 7:21, 25. “Every tribe, and people, and tongue, and nation”: cf. 5:9; 7:9; 14:6; the Textus Receptus omits “and people”.

verses.text: And all who dwell on the earth will worship it, everyone whose name is not written in the book of life of the slain Lamb from the foundation of the world.
verses.note: “Worship it”: Gr. αὐτόν, masculine. “Book of life”: cf. 3:5; 17:8; 20:12, 15; 21:27. Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read ὧν, “all whose name” (the Textus Receptus, “whose names”). “From the foundation of the world”: alternative reading: it goes with “written”, “whose name is not written from the foundation of the world” (cf. 17:8).

verses.text: If anyone has an ear, let him hear.
If anyone is for captivity, into captivity he goes; if anyone is to be killed with the sword, with the sword he is to be killed. Here is the perseverance and the faith of the saints.
verses.note: Lit. “if anyone for captivity, into captivity he goes; if anyone with the sword to be killed, he with the sword to be killed”. Cf. Jer 15:2; 43:11 [LXX 50:11]. The SBLGNT is followed, with Codex Alexandrinus. Variants: codices Sinaiticus and Ephraemi, the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “if anyone kills with the sword, he must be killed with the sword”; in the first clause, the Textus Receptus reads “if anyone gathers captives, into captivity he goes”, and the Byzantine text, “if anyone has captivity, he goes”. “Perseverance”: Gr. ὑπομονή (cf. 1:9; 14:12).

verses.text: And I saw another beast coming up out of the earth, and it had two horns like those of a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon.
verses.note: “Lamb”: Gr. ἀρνίον, the same term as in 5:6; here in a comparison, without the article, and so in lowercase. “Out of the earth”: in contrast with “out of the sea” (13:1).

verses.text: It exercises all the authority of the first beast in its presence, and makes the earth and those who dwell in it worship the first beast, whose mortal wound was healed.
verses.note: “Exercises”: Gr. ποιεῖ, lit. “does”. “In its presence”: Gr. ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.

verses.text: It performs great signs, so that it even makes fire come down from heaven to the earth in the presence of men.
verses.note: “Signs”: Gr. σημεῖα (cf. 16:14; 19:20). “Fire… from heaven”: cf. 1 Kgs 18:38; 2 Kgs 1:10.

verses.text: And it deceives those who dwell on the earth because of the signs that it was granted to perform in the presence of the beast, telling those who dwell on the earth to make an image to the beast that has the wound of the sword and came to life.
verses.note: “Deceives”: Gr. πλανάω (cf. 12:9; 19:20). “Image”: Gr. εἰκών (cf. Dan 3:1–7). “That has”: Gr. ὅς, masculine; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read ὅ, neuter. “Came to life”: Gr. ἔζησεν (cf. 2:8; 20:4).

verses.text: It was granted to give breath to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast would even speak and would cause all who would not worship the image of the beast to be killed.
verses.note: “Breath”: Gr. πνεῦμα (cf. 11:11). “All who would not worship… to be killed”: cf. Dan 3:6, 15.

verses.text: It causes all, the small and the great, and the rich and the poor, and the free and the slaves, to be given a mark on their right hand or on their forehead,
verses.note: “The small and the great”: cf. 11:18; 19:5, 18; 20:12. “Slaves”: Gr. δοῦλοι, beside “free” (cf. 6:15). “Mark”: Gr. χάραγμα (cf. 14:9, 11; 16:2; 19:20; 20:4). Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “that he give them”, singular. “Right hand… forehead”: cf. 7:3; 14:1; Deut 6:8.

verses.text: and that no one may be able to buy or sell except the one who has the mark, the name of the beast or the number of its name.
verses.note: “Buy or sell”: Gr. ἀγοράζω (cf. 3:18; 5:9). “The number of its name”: cf. 15:2. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “or the name”.

verses.text: Here is wisdom. Let the one who has understanding calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man; and its number is six hundred and sixty-six.
verses.note: “Understanding”: Gr. νοῦς (cf. 17:9). “Calculate”: Gr. ψηφισάτω, “count, calculate”. “The number of a man”: Gr. ἀριθμὸς ἀνθρώπου, without the article; also “a human number”. “Six hundred and sixty-six”: so Papyrus 47 and codices Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus. Variant: Codex Ephraemi and Papyrus 115 read “six hundred and sixteen”.

blocks.text: The beast that rises from the sea

segments.text: And I saw a beast coming up out of the sea, having ten horns and seven heads, and on its horns ten diadems, and on its heads names of blasphemy.
The beast that I saw was like a leopard, and its feet were like those of a bear, and its mouth like the mouth of a lion. The dragon gave it his power, and his throne, and great authority.
And one of its heads was as though slain to death, and its mortal wound was healed. And the whole earth marveled, following the beast,
and they worshiped the dragon, because he had given his authority to the beast; and they worshiped the beast, saying: Who is like the beast? And who is able to make war against it?
A mouth was given to it, speaking great things and blasphemies, and authority was given to it to act for forty-two months.
It opened its mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme His name and His tabernacle, those who have their tabernacle in heaven.
And it was granted to make war against the saints and to conquer them; and authority was given to it over every tribe, and people, and tongue, and nation.
And all who dwell on the earth will worship it, everyone whose name is not written in the book of life of the slain Lamb from the foundation of the world.
If anyone has an ear, let him hear.
If anyone is for captivity, into captivity he goes;
if anyone is to be killed with the sword, with the sword he is to be killed.
Here is the perseverance and the faith of the saints.

blocks.text: The beast that rises from the earth

segments.text: And I saw another beast coming up out of the earth, and it had two horns like those of a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon.
It exercises all the authority of the first beast in its presence, and makes the earth and those who dwell in it worship the first beast, whose mortal wound was healed.
It performs great signs, so that it even makes fire come down from heaven to the earth in the presence of men.

And it deceives those who dwell on the earth because of the signs that it was granted to perform in the presence of the beast, telling those who dwell on the earth to make an image to the beast that has the wound of the sword and came to life.
It was granted to give breath to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast would even speak and would cause all who would not worship the image of the beast to be killed.
It causes all, the small and the great, and the rich and the poor, and the free and the slaves, to be given a mark on their right hand or on their forehead,
and that no one may be able to buy or sell except the one who has the mark, the name of the beast or the number of its name.
Here is wisdom. Let the one who has understanding calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man; and its number is six hundred and sixty-six.

headings.text: The Lamb and the one hundred and forty-four thousand
The messages of the three angels

verses.text: And I saw, and behold, the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him one hundred and forty-four thousand, who had His name and the name of His Father written on their foreheads.
verses.note: “Mount Zion”: cf. Ps 2:6; Isa 24:23; Joel 2:32 (Heb. 3:5); Heb 12:22. “His name and the name of His Father”: cf. 3:12; 7:3; 22:4; the Textus Receptus omits “His name and”. Variant: the Byzantine text reads “a number of one hundred and forty-four thousand”; the Textus Receptus reads “a Lamb”.

verses.text: And I heard a voice from heaven, like the voice of many waters and like the voice of loud thunder; and the voice that I heard was like that of harpists playing their harps.
verses.note: “Voice of many waters”: cf. 1:15; 19:6; Ezek 43:2. “Harpists playing their harps”: Gr. κιθαρῳδῶν κιθαριζόντων ἐν ταῖς κιθάραις (cf. 5:8; 15:2).

verses.text: They sing as it were a new song before the throne, and before the four living creatures and the elders; and no one could learn the song except the one hundred and forty-four thousand, those who had been purchased from the earth.
verses.note: “As it were a new song”: Gr. ὡς ᾠδὴν καινήν (cf. 5:9; 15:3); the Byzantine text omits “as it were”. “Purchased”: Gr. ἀγοράζω (cf. 5:9).

verses.text: These are the ones who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins. These are the ones who follow the Lamb wherever He goes. These were purchased from among men as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb,
verses.note: “Virgins”: Gr. παρθένοι, here applied to men (οὗτοι) (cf. 2 Cor 11:2). “Follow the Lamb”: cf. John 10:4, 27. “Firstfruits”: Gr. ἀπαρχή (cf. Jer 2:3; Jas 1:18). Variant: the Byzantine text reads “these were purchased by Jesus”.

verses.text: and in their mouth no lie was found; they are blameless.
verses.note: “Lie”: Gr. ψεῦδος; the Textus Receptus reads “deceit” and adds “before the throne of God”. Cf. Zeph 3:13; Isa 53:9. “Blameless”: Gr. ἄμωμοι, “without blemish” (cf. Ex 29:1; 1 Pet 1:19); the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “for they are blameless”.

verses.text: And I saw another angel flying in midheaven, having the eternal gospel to proclaim to those who sit on the earth, and to every nation, and tribe, and tongue, and people,
verses.note: “Flying in midheaven”: cf. 8:13. “The eternal gospel”: Gr. εὐαγγέλιον αἰώνιον, without the article in the Greek. “Proclaim”: Gr. εὐαγγελίσαι, “announce the good news” (cf. 10:7), here with “gospel” as its object. “Sit”: Gr. καθημένους, lit. “seated”; Papyrus 115, Codex Alexandrinus and the Textus Receptus read “dwell”. “Every nation, and tribe, and tongue, and people”: cf. 5:9; 13:7. Variant: the Byzantine text omits “another”.

verses.text: saying with a loud voice: Fear God and give Him glory, because the hour of His judgment has come; and worship Him who made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and the springs of waters.
verses.note: “Fear God and give Him glory”: cf. 11:13; 15:4; Eccl 12:13; Jer 13:16; the Byzantine text reads “Fear the Lord”. “Judgment”: Gr. κρίσις (cf. 16:7; 18:10; 19:2; Dan 7:10, 22, 26). “Him who made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and the springs of waters”: cf. Ex 20:11; Ps 146:6 [LXX 145:6]; Acts 14:15; Rev 10:6; the SBLGNT has no article before “sea” and “springs”; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “the sea”.

verses.text: And another angel, a second, followed, saying: Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, which made all the nations drink of the wine of the fury of her prostitution.
verses.note: “Another angel, a second”: Gr. ἄλλος δεύτερος ἄγγελος. “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great”: cf. 18:2; Isa 21:9; Jer 51:7–8 [LXX 28:7–8]; Dan 4:30 (Heb. 4:27). “Fury”: Gr. θυμός, also “passion” (cf. 12:12; 18:3). “Made… drink”: Gr. πεπότικεν, perfect. Variants: the Textus Receptus omits “a second” and reads “Babylon the city, the great, because she made… drink”; the Byzantine text has “fallen” only once.

verses.text: And another angel, a third, followed them, saying with a loud voice: If anyone worships the beast and its image, and receives the mark on his forehead or on his hand,
verses.note: “Worships… receives”: presents in the Greek. “The mark”: Gr. χάραγμα, without the article in the Greek; it is the mark of the beast (cf. 13:16–17; 14:11).

verses.text: he too will drink of the wine of the fury of God, prepared undiluted in the cup of His wrath; and he will be tormented with fire and sulfur before holy angels and before the Lamb.
verses.note: “Prepared undiluted”: Gr. κεκερασμένου ἀκράτου, lit. “mixed unmixed”. “Holy angels”: without the article; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “the holy angels”. “Cup of His wrath”: cf. 16:19; Ps 75:8 (Heb. 75:9) [LXX 74:9]; Isa 51:17; Jer 25:15 [LXX 32:1]. “Fire and sulfur”: cf. 19:20; 20:10; 21:8; Gen 19:24.

verses.text: And the smoke of their torment goes up forever and ever; and they have no rest, day and night, those who worship the beast and its image, and whoever receives the mark of its name.
verses.note: “Forever and ever”: Gr. εἰς αἰῶνας αἰώνων, without articles (cf. 1:6). Cf. Isa 34:9–10; Jude 7. “Rest”: Gr. ἀνάπαυσις (cf. 4:8).

verses.text: Here is the perseverance of the saints, those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.
verses.note: “Perseverance”: Gr. ὑπομονή (cf. 1:9; 13:10). “Those who keep the commandments of God”: cf. 12:17. “The faith of Jesus”: Gr. τὴν πίστιν Ἰησοῦ; alternative reading: “faith in Jesus” (cf. 2:13). Variant: the Textus Receptus repeats “here”: “here are those who keep”.

verses.text: And I heard a voice from heaven, saying: Write: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on. Yes, says the Spirit, so that they may rest from their labors, for their works follow them.
verses.note: “Write”: cf. 1:11, 19; 19:9; 21:5. “Blessed”: cf. 1:3; 16:15; 19:9; 20:6; 22:7, 14. “From now on”: Gr. ἀπ’ ἄρτι; alternative reading: it goes with what follows, “From now on, yes, says the Spirit”. “Rest”: Gr. ἀναπαήσονται (cf. 6:11). “Labors”: Gr. κόποι (cf. 2:2). “For their works follow them”: lit. “follow with them”. Variants: the Textus Receptus reads “saying to me”; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “and their works”.

verses.text: And I saw, and behold, a white cloud, and on the cloud One seated, like a Son of Man, having on His head a golden crown and in His hand a sharp sickle.
verses.note: “White cloud”: cf. 1:7; Matt 24:30. “One… like a Son of Man”: Gr. ὅμοιον υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου (cf. 1:13; Dan 7:13). The capital identifies the figure with the One “like a Son of Man” of 1:13, who comes “with the clouds” (1:7); here He also wears a golden crown. Another reading sees here an angel, since the order to reap comes from “another angel” (14:15). “Crown”: Gr. στέφανος. “Sickle”: Gr. δρέπανον.

verses.text: And another angel came out of the sanctuary, crying out with a loud voice to Him who sat on the cloud: Thrust in Your sickle and reap, because the hour to reap has come, because the harvest of the earth is ripe.
verses.note: “Sanctuary”: Gr. ναός (cf. 11:19). “Thrust in”: Gr. πέμψον, lit. “send”. “The harvest… is ripe”: Gr. ἐξηράνθη, lit. “has dried”. Cf. Joel 3:13 (Heb. 4:13); Matt 13:30, 39; Mark 4:29. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “the hour has come for You”.

verses.text: Then He who sat on the cloud cast His sickle on the earth, and the earth was reaped.
And another angel came out of the sanctuary that is in heaven, he too having a sharp sickle.
verses.note: “He too”: Gr. καὶ αὐτός.

verses.text: And another angel, the one who had authority over the fire, came out from the altar and called with a loud voice to the one who had the sharp sickle, saying: Thrust in your sharp sickle and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth, because its grapes are ripe.
verses.note: “Came out from the altar”: the verb is implied in the SBLGNT (cf. 14:17); the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus have ἐξῆλθεν and read “with a loud cry”. “Authority over the fire”: cf. 8:3–5. “Gather”: Gr. τρύγησον, “harvest grapes”. Cf. Joel 3:13 (Heb. 4:13).

verses.text: Then the angel cast his sickle to the earth, gathered the vine of the earth, and cast it into the great winepress of the fury of God.
verses.note: “Winepress of the fury of God”: cf. 19:15; Isa 63:1–6; Lam 1:15.

verses.text: The winepress was trodden outside the city, and blood came out of the winepress up to the bridles of the horses, for one thousand six hundred stadia.
verses.note: Cf. Joel 3:12–14 (Heb. 4:12–14). “One thousand six hundred stadia”: about 300 kilometers (about 185 miles); one stadion, about 185 meters (607 feet).

blocks.text: The Lamb and the one hundred and forty-four thousand

segments.text: And I saw, and behold, the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him one hundred and forty-four thousand, who had His name and the name of His Father written on their foreheads.
And I heard a voice from heaven, like the voice of many waters and like the voice of loud thunder; and the voice that I heard was like that of harpists playing their harps.

They sing as it were a new song before the throne, and before the four living creatures and the elders; and no one could learn the song except the one hundred and forty-four thousand, those who had been purchased from the earth.

These are the ones who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins. These are the ones who follow the Lamb wherever He goes. These were purchased from among men as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb,
and in their mouth no lie was found; they are blameless.

saying with a loud voice:
Fear God and give Him glory,
because the hour of His judgment has come;
and worship Him who made heaven, and earth,

And another angel, a second, followed, saying:

which made all the nations drink
of the wine of the fury of her prostitution.
And another angel, a third, followed them, saying with a loud voice: If anyone worships the beast and its image, and receives the mark on his forehead or on his hand,
he too will drink of the wine of the fury of God, prepared undiluted in the cup of His wrath; and he will be tormented with fire and sulfur before holy angels and before the Lamb.

Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.
Yes, says the Spirit, so that they may rest from their labors,

Then the angel cast his sickle to the earth, gathered the vine of the earth, and cast it into the great winepress of the fury of God.
The winepress was trodden outside the city, and blood came out of the winepress up to the bridles of the horses, for one thousand six hundred stadia.

headings.text: The song of Moses and of the Lamb
The seven angels with the seven plagues

verses.text: And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvelous: seven angels who had the seven last plagues, because in them the fury of God was completed.
verses.note: “Sign”: Gr. σημεῖον (cf. 12:1, 3). “The seven last plagues”: Gr. πληγὰς ἑπτὰ τὰς ἐσχάτας (cf. 16:1; 21:9; Lev 26:21). “Was completed”: Gr. ἐτελέσθη (cf. 10:7). “Fury”: Gr. θυμός (cf. 14:10).

verses.text: And I saw as it were a sea of glass mixed with fire, and the conquerors of the beast, and of its image, and of the number of its name, standing on the sea of glass, having harps of God.
verses.note: “As it were a sea of glass”: cf. 4:6. “The conquerors of the beast”: Gr. τοὺς νικῶντας ἐκ τοῦ θηρίου, lit. “those who conquer from the beast”. “Number of its name”: cf. 13:17–18; the Textus Receptus adds “and of its mark”. “Standing on”: Gr. ἐπί with the accusative, also “beside”. “Harps of God”: cf. 5:8; 14:2.

verses.text: They sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying: Great and marvelous are Your works, O Lord God, the Almighty; just and true are Your ways, O King of the nations.
verses.note: “The song of Moses”: cf. Ex 15:1–18; Deut 31:30–32:43. “Servant of God”: cf. Num 12:7; Josh 1:2. “Great and marvelous are Your works”: cf. Ps 111:2 [LXX 110:2]; 139:14 [LXX 138:14]. “Just and true are Your ways”: cf. Deut 32:4; Ps 145:17 [LXX 144:17]. “King of the nations”: Gr. ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν ἐθνῶν, following Codex Alexandrinus and the Byzantine text (cf. 15:4; Jer 10:7); the SBLGNT follows Papyrus 47, the original text of Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Ephraemi, which read “King of the ages” (cf. 1 Tim 1:17). Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “King of the saints”.

verses.text: Who will not fear You, O Lord, and glorify Your name? For You alone are holy; for all the nations will come and worship before You, for Your righteous acts have been made manifest.
verses.note: “Who will not fear You”: Gr. οὐ μή, an emphatic negation, which also governs “glorify”; cf. Jer 10:7 (not in the LXX). “You” is not in the SBLGNT; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read σε. “Holy”: Gr. ὅσιος (cf. 16:5); the Byzantine text reads ἅγιος. “All the nations will come and worship”: cf. Ps 86:9 [LXX 85:9]; Isa 2:2–3; 66:23. “Righteous acts”: Gr. δικαιώματα (cf. 19:8). “Have been made manifest”: Gr. ἐφανερώθησαν.

verses.text: And after these things I saw, and the sanctuary of the tabernacle of the testimony was opened in heaven,
verses.note: “The sanctuary of the tabernacle of the testimony”: Gr. ὁ ναὸς τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου (cf. 11:19; Ex 38:21 [LXX 37:19]; Num 1:50; Acts 7:44). Variant: the Textus Receptus adds “and behold”.

verses.text: and the seven angels who had the seven plagues came out of the sanctuary, clothed in pure and bright linen, and girded at the chest with golden sashes.
verses.note: “Pure and bright linen”: Gr. λίνον καθαρὸν λαμπρόν (cf. 19:8, 14); codices Alexandrinus and Ephraemi read λίθον, “stone” (cf. Ezek 28:13). “Girded at the chest with golden sashes”: cf. 1:13; Dan 10:5.

verses.text: Then one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the fury of God, who lives forever and ever.
verses.note: “Bowls”: Gr. φιάλας (cf. 5:8; 16:1). “Who lives forever and ever”: cf. 4:9–10; 10:6.

verses.text: The sanctuary was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power; and no one could enter the sanctuary until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.
verses.note: “From the glory”: Gr. ἐκ τῆς δόξης. “The sanctuary was filled with smoke”: cf. Ex 40:34–35 [LXX 40:28–29]; 1 Kgs 8:10–11; 2 Chr 5:13–14; Isa 6:4. “Were completed”: Gr. τελεσθῶσιν (cf. 15:1).

blocks.text: The song of Moses and of the Lamb

segments.text: And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvelous: seven angels who had the seven last plagues, because in them the fury of God was completed.
And I saw as it were a sea of glass mixed with fire, and the conquerors of the beast, and of its image, and of the number of its name, standing on the sea of glass, having harps of God.
They sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying:
Great and marvelous are Your works,
O Lord God, the Almighty;
just and true are Your ways,
O King of the nations.
Who will not fear You, O Lord,
and glorify Your name?
For You alone are holy;
for all the nations will come
and worship before You,
for Your righteous acts have been made manifest.

blocks.text: The seven angels with the seven plagues

segments.text: And after these things I saw, and the sanctuary of the tabernacle of the testimony was opened in heaven,
and the seven angels who had the seven plagues came out of the sanctuary, clothed in pure and bright linen, and girded at the chest with golden sashes.
Then one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the fury of God, who lives forever and ever.
The sanctuary was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power; and no one could enter the sanctuary until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.

headings.text: The seven bowls of the wrath of God

verses.text: And I heard a loud voice from the sanctuary, saying to the seven angels: Go and pour out on the earth the seven bowls of the fury of God.
verses.note: “A loud voice from the sanctuary”: Gr. ναός (cf. 15:5–8). “Pour out”: Gr. ἐκχέετε. “Bowls of the fury of God”: cf. 15:1, 7. Cf. Ex 7–10.

verses.text: And the first went and poured out his bowl on the earth: a bad and malignant sore came upon the men who had the mark of the beast and who worshiped its image.
verses.note: “A bad and malignant sore”: Gr. ἕλκος κακὸν καὶ πονηρόν (cf. Ex 9:9–11; Deut 28:35). “The mark of the beast… its image”: cf. 13:15–17; 14:9–11.

verses.text: And the second poured out his bowl into the sea: it became blood like that of a dead man, and every living soul that was in the sea died.
verses.note: “It became blood”: lit. “there came blood”. “Blood like that of a dead man”: cf. 8:8–9; Ex 7:17–21. “Every living soul”: Gr. πᾶσα ψυχὴ ζωῆς, lit. “every soul of life” (cf. Gen 1:21); the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read ψυχὴ ζῶσα.

verses.text: And the third poured out his bowl into the rivers and the springs of waters: they became blood.
verses.note: “They became blood”: lit. “there came blood” (cf. Ex 7:19–21; Ps 78:44 [LXX 77:44]).

verses.text: And I heard the angel of the waters saying: Just are You, Who Is, and Who Was, the Holy One, because You have judged these things;
verses.note: “The angel of the waters”: cf. 7:1; 14:18. “Just are You”: cf. 15:3; Deut 32:4; Ps 119:137 [LXX 118:137]. “Who Is, and Who Was”: cf. 1:4, 8; 11:17. “The Holy One”: Gr. ὁ ὅσιος (cf. 15:4); the Textus Receptus reads “Just are You, O Lord, who is, and who was, and who shall be”.

verses.text: because they poured out the blood of saints and of prophets, and You have given them blood to drink; they deserve it.
verses.note: “Blood of saints and of prophets”: cf. 17:6; 18:24. “You have given them blood to drink”: cf. Isa 49:26. “They deserve it”: Gr. ἄξιοί εἰσιν, lit. “they are worthy” (cf. 3:4); the Textus Receptus reads “for they are worthy”.

verses.text: And I heard the altar saying: Yes, O Lord God, the Almighty, true and just are Your judgments.
verses.note: “I heard the altar saying”: cf. 6:9–10; 8:3–5; 9:13; the Textus Receptus reads “I heard another, from the altar, saying”. “Yes”: Gr. ναί (cf. 1:7). “True and just are Your judgments”: Gr. κρίσεις (cf. 15:3; 19:2).

verses.text: And the fourth poured out his bowl on the sun: it was granted to it to scorch men with fire.
verses.note: “Scorch”: Gr. καυματίσαι (cf. 7:16).

verses.text: Men were scorched with great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God, who has authority over these plagues, and they did not repent to give Him glory.
verses.note: “Heat”: Gr. καῦμα (cf. 7:16). “Blasphemed”: cf. 13:6; 16:11, 21. “Did not repent”: cf. 2:21; 9:20–21. “Give Him glory”: cf. 11:13; 14:7.

verses.text: And the fifth poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast: its kingdom was darkened, and they gnawed their tongues because of the pain,
verses.note: “The throne of the beast”: cf. 2:13; 13:2. “Was darkened”: Gr. ἐσκοτωμένη, perfect participle (cf. Ex 10:21–23; Joel 2:31 (Heb. 3:4)).

verses.text: and they blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and they did not repent of their works.
verses.note: “The God of heaven”: cf. 11:13; Dan 2:18–19, 44. “Sores”: cf. 16:2.

verses.text: And the sixth poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates: its water dried up, so that the way of the kings from the rising of the sun might be prepared.
verses.note: “The great river Euphrates”: cf. 9:14. “Its water dried up”: cf. Isa 11:15; 44:27; Jer 50:38 [LXX 27:38]; 51:36 [LXX 28:36]. “The kings from the rising of the sun”: cf. 7:2; Isa 41:2, 25; 46:11; the Textus Receptus reads “risings” in the plural.

verses.text: And I saw coming out of the mouth of the dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits like frogs;
verses.note: “The false prophet”: Gr. ψευδοπροφήτης (cf. 13:11–14; 19:20; 20:10). “I saw coming out of the mouth”: lit. “I saw out of the mouth”. “Unclean spirits”: Gr. πνεύματα ἀκάθαρτα. “Like frogs”: Gr. ὡς βάτραχοι (cf. Ex 8:2–7 (Heb. 7:27–8:3)); the Textus Receptus reads ὅμοια βατράχοις, “resembling frogs”.

verses.text: for they are spirits of demons, performing signs, who go out to the kings of the whole world, to gather them for the war of the great day of God, the Almighty —
verses.note: “Demons”: Gr. δαιμόνια (cf. 9:20). “Signs”: Gr. σημεῖα (cf. 13:13–14; 19:20). “Whole world”: Gr. οἰκουμένη ὅλη (cf. 3:10; 12:9). “Gather them for the war”: cf. 19:19; 20:8. “The great day of God”: cf. 6:17; Joel 2:11; 2:31 (Heb. 3:4); Zeph 1:14. Variants: the Textus Receptus reads “the kings of the earth and of the whole world”; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “of that great day”. The dash marks the parenthesis of v. 15, as in the Greek.

verses.text: Behold, I am coming like a thief. Blessed is the one who watches and keeps his garments, so that he may not walk naked and others not see his shame —
verses.note: “Behold, I am coming like a thief”: cf. 3:3; Matt 24:43; Luke 12:39; 1 Thess 5:2; 2 Pet 3:10. “Blessed”: cf. 1:3; 14:13. “Watches”: Gr. γρηγορέω (cf. 3:2–3). “Garments”: Gr. ἱμάτια (cf. 3:4–5, 18). “Shame”: Gr. ἀσχημοσύνη, lit. “indecency”, nakedness exposed (cf. 3:18, where “shame” renders αἰσχύνη).

verses.text: And they gathered them to the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon.
verses.note: “They gathered”: Gr. συνήγαγεν, singular with a neuter plural subject, the spirits (16:13–14); alternative reading: “And he gathered them”. “Armageddon”: Gr. Ἁρμαγεδών, from the Hebrew, generally understood as “mountain of Megiddo” (cf. Judg 5:19; 2 Kgs 23:29; Zech 12:11); alternative reading: “mountain of assembly” (cf. Isa 14:13); the Textus Receptus reads Ἁρμαγεδδών, the source of the familiar English spelling.

verses.text: And the seventh poured out his bowl upon the air: a loud voice came out of the sanctuary, from the throne, saying: It is done!
verses.note: “Upon the air”: the Textus Receptus reads “into the air”. “Out of the sanctuary, from the throne”: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus add “of heaven” after “sanctuary”. “It is done”: Gr. γέγονεν, perfect (cf. 21:6; also 10:7; 15:1).

verses.text: And there were flashes of lightning, and voices, and thunders, and there was a great earthquake, such as there had never been since men came to be on the earth, so great an earthquake as this.
verses.note: “Flashes of lightning, and voices, and thunders”: cf. 4:5; 8:5; 11:19. “Such as there had never been”: cf. Dan 12:1; Matt 24:21. “Since men came to be”: some manuscripts read “man”, singular. “So great an earthquake as this”: Gr. τηλικοῦτος σεισμὸς οὕτω μέγας, lit. “such an earthquake, so great”.

verses.text: And the great city was split into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell; and Babylon the great was remembered before God, to give her the cup of the wine of the fury of His wrath.
verses.note: “The great city”: cf. 11:8; 17:18; 18:10. “Was split into three parts”: lit. “came to be in three parts”. “Was remembered before God”: Gr. ἐμνήσθη ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ (cf. 18:5). “The cup of the wine of the fury of His wrath”: cf. 14:8, 10; 18:3; Jer 25:15 [LXX 32:1].

verses.text: And every island fled away, and the mountains were not found.
And great hail, about the weight of a talent, comes down from heaven upon men; and men blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail, for its plague is exceedingly great.
verses.note: “Hail”: cf. 8:7; 11:19; Ex 9:23–25. “About the weight of a talent”: Gr. ὡς ταλαντιαία, “weighing a talent”, a measure of weight of about 30 to 40 kilograms (65 to 90 pounds). “Comes down”: present in the Greek. “Plague”: Gr. πληγή (cf. 9:18; 15:1).

blocks.text: The seven bowls of the wrath of God

segments.text: And I heard a loud voice from the sanctuary, saying to the seven angels: Go and pour out on the earth the seven bowls of the fury of God.
And the first went and poured out his bowl on the earth: a bad and malignant sore came upon the men who had the mark of the beast and who worshiped its image.
And the second poured out his bowl into the sea: it became blood like that of a dead man, and every living soul that was in the sea died.
And the third poured out his bowl into the rivers and the springs of waters: they became blood.
And I heard the angel of the waters saying: Just are You, Who Is, and Who Was, the Holy One, because You have judged these things;
because they poured out the blood of saints and of prophets, and You have given them blood to drink; they deserve it.
And I heard the altar saying: Yes, O Lord God, the Almighty, true and just are Your judgments.
And the fourth poured out his bowl on the sun: it was granted to it to scorch men with fire.
Men were scorched with great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God, who has authority over these plagues, and they did not repent to give Him glory.
And the fifth poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast: its kingdom was darkened, and they gnawed their tongues because of the pain,
and they blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and they did not repent of their works.
And the sixth poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates: its water dried up, so that the way of the kings from the rising of the sun might be prepared.
And I saw coming out of the mouth of the dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits like frogs;
for they are spirits of demons, performing signs, who go out to the kings of the whole world, to gather them for the war of the great day of God, the Almighty —
Behold, I am coming like a thief. Blessed is the one who watches and keeps his garments, so that he may not walk naked and others not see his shame —
And they gathered them to the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon.
And the seventh poured out his bowl upon the air: a loud voice came out of the sanctuary, from the throne, saying: It is done!
And there were flashes of lightning, and voices, and thunders, and there was a great earthquake, such as there had never been since men came to be on the earth, so great an earthquake as this.
And the great city was split into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell; and Babylon the great was remembered before God, to give her the cup of the wine of the fury of His wrath.
And every island fled away, and the mountains were not found.
And great hail, about the weight of a talent, comes down from heaven upon men; and men blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail, for its plague is exceedingly great.

headings.text: The great prostitute and the beast
The mystery of the woman and of the beast

verses.text: And one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying: Come, I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute who is seated on many waters,
verses.note: “One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls”: cf. 15:7; 21:9. “Come”: Gr. δεῦρο. “Judgment”: Gr. κρίμα (cf. 18:20; 20:4). “Prostitute”: Gr. πόρνη (cf. 17:15–16; 19:2). “Seated on many waters”: cf. 17:15; Jer 51:13 [LXX 28:13].

verses.text: with whom the kings of the earth prostituted themselves, and those who dwell on the earth became drunk with the wine of her prostitution.
verses.note: “Prostituted themselves”: Gr. πορνεύω (cf. 2:14, 20; 18:3, 9). “Became drunk with the wine of her prostitution”: cf. 14:8; 18:3; Jer 51:7 [LXX 28:7].

verses.text: And he carried me away in the Spirit into a wilderness; and I saw a woman seated on a scarlet beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns.
verses.note: “Carried me away in the Spirit”: Gr. ἀπήνεγκέν με… ἐν πνεύματι (cf. 1:10; 4:2; 21:10; Ezek 3:12, 14). “Scarlet”: Gr. κόκκινος (cf. 17:4; 18:12, 16). “Names of blasphemy”: cf. 13:1, 5–6. “Seven heads and ten horns”: cf. 12:3; 13:1.

verses.text: The woman was clothed in purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold, and precious stones, and pearls, having in her hand a golden cup full of abominations and of the impurities of her prostitution,
verses.note: “Clothed”: Gr. περιβάλλω (cf. 3:5). “Purple and scarlet”: cf. 18:16; Ex 28:5–6. “Adorned with gold”: lit. “gilded with gold”. “Golden cup”: cf. Jer 51:7 [LXX 28:7]. “Abominations”: Gr. βδελύγματα (cf. 17:5; 21:27; Dan 9:27; 11:31). “Impurities”: Gr. τὰ ἀκάθαρτα; the Textus Receptus reads “of the impurity”.

verses.text: and on her forehead a name written: Mystery, Babylon the great, the mother of the prostitutes and of the abominations of the earth.
verses.note: “On her forehead a name written”: cf. 13:16; 14:1, 9; 22:4. “Mystery”: Gr. μυστήριον, part of the name or a description of it (cf. 17:7). “Babylon the great”: cf. 14:8; 16:19; 18:2; Dan 4:30 (Heb. 4:27). “The mother of the prostitutes”: cf. Ezek 16:44–45.

verses.text: And I saw the woman drunk with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the witnesses of Jesus. When I saw her, I marveled with great amazement.
verses.note: “Drunk with the blood of the saints”: cf. 6:10; 16:6; 18:24. “Witnesses”: Gr. μάρτυρες (cf. 2:13; 11:3). “I marveled with great amazement”: Gr. ἐθαύμασα… θαῦμα μέγα, lit. “I marveled with a great marvel”.

verses.text: Then the angel said to me: Why did you marvel? I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and the ten horns.
verses.note: “Mystery”: cf. 1:20; 10:7. “Carries”: Gr. βαστάζω.

verses.text: The beast that you saw was, and is not, and is about to come up out of the abyss, and goes to destruction; and those who dwell on the earth, whose name is not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world, will marvel when they see the beast, that it was, and is not, and will come.
verses.note: “Was, and is not, and is about to come up”: cf. 1:4, 8; 4:8; 11:7. “Abyss”: cf. 9:1; 11:7. “Destruction”: Gr. ἀπώλεια (cf. 9:11). “Whose name is not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world”: cf. 13:8. “That it was”: Gr. ὅτι, object of “see”. “And will come”: Gr. καὶ παρέσται, from πάρειμι, lit. “and will be present”, not the verb ἔρχομαι of 1:4, 8; the Textus Receptus reads “and yet is”. Variants: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “and to go to destruction” and “whose names”.

verses.text: Here is the understanding that has wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains, on which the woman is seated. And they are seven kings:
verses.note: “Here is the understanding”: cf. 13:18. “Seven mountains”: Gr. ὄρη. “And they are seven kings”: alternative reading: “and there are seven kings”; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus place the phrase in 17:10.

verses.text: five have fallen, one is, the other has not yet come; and when he comes, he must remain a little while.
verses.note: “Have fallen”: Gr. ἔπεσαν. “A little while”: Gr. ὀλίγον.

verses.text: And the beast that was and is not, he also is the eighth, and is of the seven, and goes to destruction.
verses.note: “Is the eighth, and is of the seven”: Gr. ὄγδοός ἐστιν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑπτά ἐστιν. “He also”: Gr. καὶ αὐτός, masculine, although “beast” (θηρίον) is neuter. “Is of the seven”: also “comes from the seven” or “is one of the seven”.

verses.text: And the ten horns that you saw are ten kings, who have not yet received a kingdom, but receive authority as kings for one hour, with the beast.
verses.note: “Ten horns… ten kings”: cf. 13:1; Dan 7:7, 20, 24. “One hour”: cf. 18:10, 17, 19.

verses.text: These have one purpose, and they give their power and authority to the beast.
verses.note: “One purpose”: Gr. μίαν γνώμην, lit. “one opinion”.

verses.text: These will make war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will conquer them, because He is Lord of lords and King of kings; and those who are with Him are called, and chosen, and faithful.
verses.note: “Will make war against the Lamb”: cf. 16:14; 19:19. “Lord of lords and King of kings”: cf. 19:16; Deut 10:17; Dan 2:47; 1 Tim 6:15. “And those who are with Him are called, and chosen, and faithful”: the Greek has no verb; alternative reading: “and those with Him, called, and chosen, and faithful, will also conquer them” (cf. 2:10; 19:9, 14; Matt 22:14). “Lord of lords”: without articles in the Greek.

verses.text: And he says to me: The waters that you saw, where the prostitute is seated, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.
verses.note: “Peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues”: cf. 5:9; 7:9; 10:11; 13:7; 14:6.

verses.text: And the ten horns that you saw, and the beast, these will hate the prostitute, and will make her desolate and naked, and will eat her flesh, and will burn her with fire.
verses.note: “And the beast”: the Textus Receptus reads “that you saw upon the beast”. “Will hate the prostitute”: cf. Ezek 16:37–41; 23:25–29. “Will eat her flesh”: cf. 19:18; 2 Kgs 9:36. “Will burn her with fire”: cf. 18:8; Lev 21:9.

verses.text: For God has put it into their hearts to carry out His purpose, and to have one purpose, and to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled.
verses.note: “Has put it into their hearts”: Gr. ἔδωκεν εἰς τὰς καρδίας, lit. “gave into their hearts”. “Carry out”: Gr. ποιῆσαι, “do”. “His purpose”: Gr. αὐτοῦ, God’s. “Their kingdom”: Gr. αὐτῶν, that of the ten kings. “Purpose”: Gr. γνώμη (cf. 17:13). “Are fulfilled”: Gr. τελεσθήσονται (cf. 10:7; 15:1). “Words of God”: Gr. οἱ λόγοι τοῦ θεοῦ; the Textus Receptus reads τὰ ῥήματα.

verses.text: And the woman that you saw is the great city that reigns over the kings of the earth.
verses.note: “The great city”: cf. 11:8; 16:19; 18:10. “That reigns”: Gr. ἡ ἔχουσα βασιλείαν, lit. “that has a kingdom”.

blocks.text: The great prostitute and the beast

segments.text: And one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying: Come, I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute who is seated on many waters,
with whom the kings of the earth prostituted themselves, and those who dwell on the earth became drunk with the wine of her prostitution.
And he carried me away in the Spirit into a wilderness; and I saw a woman seated on a scarlet beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns.
The woman was clothed in purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold, and precious stones, and pearls, having in her hand a golden cup full of abominations and of the impurities of her prostitution,
and on her forehead a name written: Mystery, Babylon the great, the mother of the prostitutes and of the abominations of the earth.
And I saw the woman drunk with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the witnesses of Jesus. When I saw her, I marveled with great amazement.

blocks.text: The mystery of the woman and of the beast

segments.text: Then the angel said to me: Why did you marvel? I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and the ten horns.

The beast that you saw was, and is not, and is about to come up out of the abyss, and goes to destruction; and those who dwell on the earth, whose name is not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world, will marvel when they see the beast, that it was, and is not, and will come.
Here is the understanding that has wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains, on which the woman is seated. And they are seven kings:
five have fallen, one is, the other has not yet come; and when he comes, he must remain a little while.
And the beast that was and is not, he also is the eighth, and is of the seven, and goes to destruction.
And the ten horns that you saw are ten kings, who have not yet received a kingdom, but receive authority as kings for one hour, with the beast.
These have one purpose, and they give their power and authority to the beast.
These will make war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will conquer them, because He is Lord of lords and King of kings; and those who are with Him are called, and chosen, and faithful.
And he says to me: The waters that you saw, where the prostitute is seated, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.
And the ten horns that you saw, and the beast, these will hate the prostitute, and will make her desolate and naked, and will eat her flesh, and will burn her with fire.
For God has put it into their hearts to carry out His purpose, and to have one purpose, and to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled.
And the woman that you saw is the great city that reigns over the kings of the earth.

headings.text: Come out of her, My people

verses.text: After these things I saw another angel coming down from heaven, having great authority, and the earth was illuminated by his glory.
verses.note: “Another angel”: cf. 10:1; 14:6, 8. “The earth was illuminated by his glory”: cf. Ezek 43:2.

verses.text: He cried out with a mighty voice, saying: Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, and has become a dwelling place of demons, and a prison of every unclean spirit, and a prison of every unclean bird, and a prison of every unclean and hated beast,
verses.note: “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great”: cf. 14:8; Isa 21:9; Jer 51:8 [LXX 28:8]. “A dwelling place of demons… a prison”: Gr. φυλακή, also “haunt, lair” (cf. Isa 13:21–22; 34:11–15; Jer 50:39 [LXX 27:39]; 51:37 [LXX 28:37]). “Mighty voice”: Gr. ἰσχυρᾷ φωνῇ; the Textus Receptus reads “mightily, with a loud voice”. “Beast”: Gr. θηρίον, here the wild animal (cf. 6:8). “Hated”: Gr. μεμισημένου, participle. “And a prison of every unclean and hated beast”: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus omit “a prison of every unclean… beast”, reading “every unclean and hated bird”. Variant: the Byzantine text has “fallen” only once.

verses.text: because all the nations have drunk of the wine of the fury of her prostitution, and the kings of the earth prostituted themselves with her, and the merchants of the earth grew rich from the power of her luxury.
verses.note: “Have drunk”: Gr. πέπωκαν (the Textus Receptus πέπωκε), following the Latin Vulgate, some manuscripts and the Textus Receptus (cf. 14:8; 17:2); the SBLGNT follows codices Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Ephraemi, which read πέπτωκαν, and the Byzantine text, which reads πεπτώκασιν, both “have fallen”. “Merchants”: Gr. ἔμποροι (cf. Ezek 27:12–36). “Luxury”: Gr. στρῆνος, “sensual excess, opulence”.

verses.text: And I heard another voice from heaven, saying: Come out of her, My people, so that you do not share in her sins and so that you do not receive any of her plagues;
verses.note: “Come out of her, My people… share… receive”: in the Greek, all the verbs are plural (ἐξέλθατε… συγκοινωνήσητε… λάβητε). Codex Ephraemi and the Byzantine text read ἔξελθε, singular (cf. Isa 48:20; 52:11; Jer 50:8 [LXX 27:8]; 51:6 [LXX 28:6]; 51:45 (not in the LXX); 2 Cor 6:17).

verses.text: for her sins have piled up to heaven, and God has remembered her iniquities.
verses.note: “Have piled up”: Gr. ἐκολλήθησαν, lit. “have stuck together, have been joined” (cf. Gen 18:20; Jer 51:9 [LXX 28:9]). “Has remembered”: cf. 16:19.

verses.text: Repay her as she herself repaid, and give her double according to her works; in the cup in which she mixed, mix her double.
verses.note: “Repay her as she herself repaid”: cf. Ps 137:8 [LXX 136:8]; Jer 50:15, 29 [LXX 27:15, 29]. “Give her double”: Gr. διπλώσατε τὰ διπλᾶ, lit. “double the double” (cf. Isa 40:2; Jer 16:18); the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “double to her”. “Mixed… mix”: Gr. κεράννυμι (cf. 14:10, “prepared”). Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “as she repaid you”.

verses.text: As much as she glorified herself and lived in luxury, so much torment and mourning give her; for she says in her heart: I sit as a queen, and I am not a widow, and I will never see mourning.
verses.note: “Lived in luxury”: Gr. στρηνιάω (cf. 18:3, 9). “Mourning”: Gr. πένθος. “I sit as a queen, and I am not a widow”: cf. Isa 47:7–9; Zeph 2:15 [LXX 3:1].

verses.text: Therefore in one day her plagues will come: pestilence, and mourning, and famine; and she will be burned with fire, for strong is the Lord God who judged her.
verses.note: “Pestilence”: Gr. θάνατος, lit. “death” (cf. 6:8). “In one day”: cf. Isa 47:9. “She will be burned with fire”: cf. 17:16. “Strong is the Lord God”: cf. Jer 50:34 [LXX 27:34].

verses.text: The kings of the earth, who prostituted themselves and lived in luxury with her, will weep and wail over her when they see the smoke of her burning,
verses.note: “Wail”: Gr. κόπτομαι, lit. “beat the breast” (cf. 1:7, “mourn”; Ezek 26:16–17; 27:30–35). “Burning”: Gr. πύρωσις (cf. 18:18).

verses.text: standing far off because of the fear of her torment, saying: Woe, woe, the great city, Babylon, the strong city, because in one hour your judgment has come!
verses.note: “Woe, woe”: Gr. οὐαὶ οὐαί (cf. 18:16, 19). “In one hour”: cf. 17:12; 18:17, 19. “Judgment”: Gr. κρίσις (cf. 14:7).

verses.text: The merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, because no one buys their cargo anymore:
verses.note: “Cargo”: Gr. γόμος (cf. Ezek 27:27). “Weep and mourn”: presents; the Byzantine text reads “will weep and will mourn”.

verses.text: cargo of gold, and of silver, and of precious stones, and of pearls, and of fine linen, and of purple, and of silk, and of scarlet; and all citron wood, and every article of ivory, and every article of most precious wood, and of bronze, and of iron, and of marble;
verses.note: “Fine linen”: Gr. βύσσινος (cf. 18:16; 19:8). “Citron wood”: Gr. ξύλον θύϊνον, an aromatic wood. “Most precious”: Gr. τιμιωτάτου. Cf. Ezek 27:12–24.

verses.text: and cinnamon, and spice, and incense, and ointment, and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and fine flour, and wheat, and cattle, and sheep; and horses, and carriages, and slaves, and souls of men.
verses.note: “Spice”: Gr. ἄμωμον, an aromatic plant; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus omit it. “Ointment”: Gr. μύρον, perfumed oil. “Frankincense”: Gr. λίβανος. “Fine flour”: Gr. σεμίδαλις. “Carriages”: Gr. ῥέδαι, four-wheeled carriages. “Slaves”: Gr. σώματα, lit. “bodies”, a term used for slaves. “Souls of men”: Gr. ψυχὰς ἀνθρώπων (cf. Ezek 27:13).

verses.text: And the fruit that your soul longed for has departed from you, and all things fine and splendid are lost to you, and they will never find them again.
verses.note: “The fruit that your soul longed for”: Gr. ἡ ὀπώρα σου τῆς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ψυχῆς, lit. “your fruit of the desire of the soul”. “Fine and splendid”: Gr. λιπαρὰ καὶ λαμπρά. “Never… again”: Gr. οὐκέτι οὐ μή. “They will never find them”: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “you will never find them”.

verses.text: The merchants of these things, who grew rich from her, will stand far off because of the fear of her torment, weeping and mourning,
verses.note: “Will stand far off”: cf. 18:10, 17.

verses.text: saying: Woe, woe, the great city, that was clothed in fine linen, and purple, and scarlet, and adorned with gold, and precious stones, and pearls,
verses.note: “Clothed in fine linen, and purple, and scarlet”: cf. 17:4.

verses.text: because in one hour such great riches have been made desolate! And every shipmaster, and everyone who sails anywhere, and sailors, and all who work the sea stood far off,
verses.note: “Have been made desolate”: Gr. ἠρημώθη (cf. 17:16; 18:19). “Shipmaster”: Gr. κυβερνήτης. “Everyone who sails anywhere”: Gr. ὁ ἐπὶ τόπον πλέων, lit. “the one who sails to a place”; the Textus Receptus reads “all the company in ships”. Cf. Ezek 27:26–36.

verses.text: and cried out as they saw the smoke of her burning, saying: Who is like the great city?
verses.note: “Cried out”: Gr. ἔκραξαν, aorist; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read ἔκραζον, “were crying out”, also in 18:19. “Who is like”: cf. 13:4; Ezek 27:32.

verses.text: They threw dust on their heads, and cried out, weeping and mourning, saying: Woe, woe, the great city, in which all who had ships at sea grew rich from her opulence, because in one hour she has been made desolate!
verses.note: “They threw dust on their heads”: cf. Josh 7:6; Ezek 27:30; Lam 2:10. “Opulence”: Gr. τιμιότης.

verses.text: Rejoice over her, O heaven, and you saints, and apostles, and prophets, because God has judged your cause against her.
verses.note: “Rejoice”: Gr. εὐφραίνου (cf. 12:12). “Saints, and apostles, and prophets”: the Textus Receptus reads “holy apostles”. “God has judged your cause against her”: Gr. ἔκρινεν… τὸ κρίμα ὑμῶν ἐξ αὐτῆς, lit. “has judged your judgment from her” (cf. 6:10; 19:2; Deut 32:43).

verses.text: Then a strong angel took up a stone like a great millstone and cast it into the sea, saying: Thus with force Babylon, the great city, will be cast down, and will never be found again.
verses.note: “Strong angel”: cf. 5:2; 10:1. “Like a great millstone”: Gr. ὡς μύλινον μέγαν. “With force”: Gr. ὁρμήματι. Cf. Jer 51:63–64 [LXX 28:63–64].

verses.text: And the voice of harpists, and of musicians, and of flute players, and of trumpeters will never be heard in you again; and no craftsman of any craft will be found in you again; and the sound of the millstone will never be heard in you again;
verses.note: “Harpists”: Gr. κιθαρῳδοί (cf. 14:2). “No craftsman of any craft”: Gr. πᾶς τεχνίτης πάσης τέχνης οὐ μή, lit. “every craftsman of every craft… not”. Cf. Isa 24:8; Jer 25:10; Ezek 26:13.

verses.text: and the light of a lamp will never shine in you again; and the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride will never be heard in you again; because your merchants were the great ones of the earth, because by your sorcery all the nations were deceived.
verses.note: “The voice of the bridegroom and of the bride”: cf. Jer 7:34; 16:9; 25:10. “The great ones of the earth”: Gr. μεγιστᾶνες (cf. 6:15). “Sorcery”: Gr. φαρμακεία (cf. 9:21; Isa 47:9, 12). “Deceived”: Gr. πλανάω (cf. 12:9; 13:14).

verses.text: And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all who have been slain on the earth.
verses.note: “Blood of prophets, and of saints”: cf. 16:6; 17:6; 19:2; Matt 23:35. “Slain”: Gr. σφάζω (cf. 6:9).

segments.text: After these things I saw another angel coming down from heaven, having great authority, and the earth was illuminated by his glory.
He cried out with a mighty voice, saying:
Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great,
and has become a dwelling place of demons,
and a prison of every unclean spirit,
and a prison of every unclean bird,
and a prison of every unclean and hated beast,
because all the nations have drunk of the wine of the fury of her prostitution,
and the kings of the earth prostituted themselves with her,
and the merchants of the earth grew rich from the power of her luxury.

blocks.text: Come out of her, My people

segments.text: And I heard another voice from heaven, saying: Come out of her, My people, so that you do not share in her sins and so that you do not receive any of her plagues;
for her sins have piled up to heaven, and God has remembered her iniquities.
Repay her as she herself repaid, and give her double according to her works; in the cup in which she mixed, mix her double.
As much as she glorified herself and lived in luxury, so much torment and mourning give her; for she says in her heart: I sit as a queen, and I am not a widow, and I will never see mourning.
