Therefore in one day her plagues will come: pestilence, and mourning, and famine; and she will be burned with fire, for strong is the Lord God who judged her.
The kings of the earth, who prostituted themselves and lived in luxury with her, will weep and wail over her when they see the smoke of her burning,
standing far off because of the fear of her torment, saying: Woe, woe, the great city, Babylon, the strong city, because in one hour your judgment has come!
The merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, because no one buys their cargo anymore:

cargo of gold, and of silver, and of precious stones, and of pearls, and of fine linen, and of purple, and of silk, and of scarlet; and all citron wood, and every article of ivory, and every article of most precious wood, and of bronze, and of iron, and of marble;
and cinnamon, and spice, and incense, and ointment, and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and fine flour, and wheat, and cattle, and sheep; and horses, and carriages, and slaves, and souls of men.
And the fruit that your soul longed for has departed from you, and all things fine and splendid are lost to you, and they will never find them again.
The merchants of these things, who grew rich from her, will stand far off because of the fear of her torment, weeping and mourning,
saying: Woe, woe, the great city, that was clothed in fine linen, and purple, and scarlet, and adorned with gold, and precious stones, and pearls,
because in one hour such great riches have been made desolate! And every shipmaster, and everyone who sails anywhere, and sailors, and all who work the sea stood far off,
and cried out as they saw the smoke of her burning, saying: Who is like the great city?

They threw dust on their heads, and cried out, weeping and mourning, saying: Woe, woe, the great city, in which all who had ships at sea grew rich from her opulence, because in one hour she has been made desolate!
Rejoice over her, O heaven, and you saints, and apostles, and prophets, because God has judged your cause against her.
Then a strong angel took up a stone like a great millstone and cast it into the sea, saying: Thus with force Babylon, the great city, will be cast down, and will never be found again.

And the voice of harpists, and of musicians, and of flute players, and of trumpeters will never be heard in you again; and no craftsman of any craft will be found in you again; and the sound of the millstone will never be heard in you again;

and the light of a lamp will never shine in you again; and the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride will never be heard in you again; because your merchants were the great ones of the earth, because by your sorcery all the nations were deceived.
And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all who have been slain on the earth.

headings.text: The Rider on the white horse

verses.text: After these things I heard as it were a loud voice of a great multitude in heaven, saying: Hallelujah! Salvation, and glory, and power belong to our God,
verses.note: “As it were a loud voice of a great multitude”: cf. 7:9–10; 19:6. “Hallelujah”: Gr. ἁλληλουϊά, from the Hebrew, “praise Yah” (cf. Ps 104:35 [LXX 103:35]; 106:1, 48 [LXX 105:1, 48]). “Belong to our God”: the Greek has no verb (cf. 7:10; also 12:10). Variant: the Textus Receptus adds “and the honor” and reads “to the Lord our God”.

verses.text: because true and just are His judgments; because He has judged the great prostitute, who corrupted the earth with her prostitution, and He has avenged the blood of His servants at her hand.
verses.note: “True and just are His judgments”: cf. 15:3; 16:7. “Corrupted”: Gr. ἔφθειρεν (cf. 11:18, διαφθείρω); the Byzantine text reads διέφθειρεν. “Has avenged the blood of His servants”: cf. 6:10; Deut 32:43; 2 Kgs 9:7. “At her hand”: that is, exacting it from her (cf. 2 Kgs 9:7; Rev 18:20).

verses.text: And they said a second time: Hallelujah! And her smoke goes up forever and ever.
verses.note: “A second time”: Gr. δεύτερον. “Said”: Gr. εἴρηκαν, perfect. “Her smoke goes up”: cf. 14:11; 18:9, 18; Isa 34:10.

verses.text: And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God, who is seated on the throne, saying: Amen! Hallelujah!
verses.note: “Fell down and worshiped”: cf. 4:10; 5:14; 11:16. “Amen! Hallelujah!”: cf. Ps 106:48 [LXX 105:48].

verses.text: And a voice came out from the throne, saying: Praise our God, all His servants, and you who fear Him, the small and the great.
verses.note: “Praise our God”: Gr. αἰνεῖτε τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν (cf. Ps 134:1 [LXX 133:1]; 135:1, 20 [LXX 134:1, 20]). “The small and the great”: cf. 11:18; 13:16; Ps 115:13 [LXX 113:21].

verses.text: And I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude, and as it were the voice of many waters, and as it were the voice of mighty thunders, saying: Hallelujah! For the Lord God, the Almighty, has begun to reign.
verses.note: “Voice of many waters… of mighty thunders”: cf. 1:15; 14:2. “Has begun to reign”: Gr. ἐβασίλευσεν, aorist (cf. 11:17; Ps 93:1 [LXX 92:1]; 97:1 [LXX 96:1]; 99:1 [LXX 98:1]). “The Lord God”: the Byzantine text reads “the Lord our God”.

verses.text: Let us rejoice and exult, and we will give Him the glory, because the wedding of the Lamb has come, and His wife has made herself ready;
verses.note: “Let us rejoice and exult”: cf. Ps 118:24 [LXX 117:24]; Matt 5:12. “And we will give”: Gr. δώσομεν, future; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “let us give”. “Wedding”: Gr. γάμος (cf. 19:9; Matt 22:2–14). “His wife”: Gr. ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ (cf. 21:2, 9; Isa 54:5–6; Hos 2:19–20 (Heb. 2:21–22)).

verses.text: and it was granted to her to clothe herself in fine linen, bright and pure; for the fine linen is the righteous acts of the saints.
verses.note: “Clothe herself”: Gr. περιβάλλω. “Fine linen”: Gr. βύσσινος (cf. 18:12, 16; 19:14; also 15:6, Gr. λίνον). “Righteous acts”: Gr. δικαιώματα (cf. 15:4). Cf. Isa 61:10.

verses.text: Then he says to me: Write: Blessed are those who have been called to the wedding supper of the Lamb. And he says to me: These words are true words of God.
verses.note: “Write”: cf. 14:13. “Blessed”: cf. 1:3; 14:13; 16:15. “Wedding supper”: cf. Matt 22:2–10; Luke 14:15–24. “Have been called”: Gr. κεκλημένοι, perfect. “These words are true words of God”: lit. “these words true of God are” (cf. 21:5; 22:6).

verses.text: And I fell down before his feet to worship him. And he says to me: See that you do not do that; I am a fellow servant of yours and of your brothers who have the Testimony of Jesus. Worship God; for the Testimony of Jesus is the Spirit of prophecy.
verses.note: “To worship him”: cf. 22:8–9. “See that you do not do that”: Gr. ὅρα μή, lit. “see, not”. “Fellow servant”: Gr. σύνδουλος (cf. 6:11; 22:9). “The Testimony of Jesus”: cf. 1:2, 9; 12:17. “The Spirit of prophecy”: Gr. τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς προφητείας; the capital follows the usage of the book, in which “the Spirit” used absolutely is the Holy Spirit (cf. 2:7; 14:13; 22:17; 1 Pet 1:10–11; 2 Pet 1:21); alternative reading: “the spirit”, that is, the essence of prophecy.

verses.text: And I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse, and He who sat on it is called Faithful and True, and in righteousness He judges and makes war.
verses.note: “He”: the capital follows the identification given by the text itself: “Faithful and True” (3:14), “the Word of God” (19:13), “King of kings and Lord of lords” (19:16; cf. 17:14). “Is called”: Gr. καλούμενος, participle. “Heaven opened”: cf. 4:1; Ezek 1:1. “White horse”: cf. 6:2. “Faithful and True”: cf. 1:5; 3:7, 14. “In righteousness He judges”: cf. Ps 96:13 [LXX 95:13]; Isa 11:4.

verses.text: His eyes are a flame of fire, and on His head are many diadems, and He has a name written that no one knows except He Himself;
verses.note: “Eyes… a flame of fire”: cf. 1:14; 2:18; Dan 10:6; the Textus Receptus adds “as”. “Diadems”: Gr. διαδήματα (cf. 12:3; 13:1). “A name written that no one knows”: cf. 2:17; 3:12. Variant: the Byzantine text adds “names written, and”.

verses.text: and He is clothed in a garment dipped in blood; and His name is called: the Word of God.
verses.note: “Clothed”: Gr. περιβάλλω. “Dipped in blood”: Gr. βεβαμμένον αἵματι (cf. Isa 63:1–3); some manuscripts read “sprinkled with blood”. “The Word of God”: Gr. ὁ Λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ (cf. John 1:1, 14; Rev 1:2, 9). “Is called”: Gr. κέκληται, perfect; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read καλεῖται.

verses.text: The armies that are in heaven followed Him on white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and pure.
verses.note: “Armies”: Gr. στρατεύματα. “Fine linen, white and pure”: cf. 19:8.

verses.text: From His mouth comes a sharp sword, so that with it He may strike the nations; and He will shepherd them with a rod of iron; and He treads the winepress of the wine of the fury of the wrath of God, the Almighty.
verses.note: “Sharp sword”: Gr. ῥομφαία ὀξεῖα (cf. 1:16; 2:12, 16; Isa 11:4; 49:2); the Byzantine text adds “two-edged”. “Strike”: Gr. πατάσσω (cf. 11:6). “Shepherd them with a rod of iron”: cf. 2:27; 12:5; Ps 2:9. “Treads the winepress”: cf. 14:19–20; Isa 63:3; Joel 3:13 (Heb. 4:13); the Textus Receptus reads “of the fury and of the wrath”.

verses.text: He has on His garment and on His thigh a name written: King of kings and Lord of lords.
verses.note: “Thigh”: Gr. μηρός. “King of kings and Lord of lords”: cf. 17:14; Deut 10:17; 1 Tim 6:15.

verses.text: And I saw an angel standing in the sun, and he cried out with a loud voice, saying to all the birds that fly in midheaven: Come, gather together for the great supper of God,
verses.note: “Birds that fly in midheaven”: cf. 8:13; 14:6. “Come, gather together”: Gr. δεῦτε συνάχθητε. “The great supper of God”: cf. Ezek 39:17–20; the Textus Receptus reads “the supper of the great God”.

verses.text: to eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of commanders, and the flesh of mighty men, and the flesh of horses and of those who sit on them, and the flesh of all, free and slaves, and small and great.
verses.note: “Commanders”: Gr. χιλίαρχοι (cf. 6:15). “Free and slaves, and small and great”: cf. 6:15; 13:16.

verses.text: And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered to make the war against Him who sat on the horse and against His army.
verses.note: “Gathered to make the war”: Gr. τὸν πόλεμον, with the article (cf. 16:14, 16; 17:14; 20:8; Ps 2:2); the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus omit the article.

verses.text: Then the beast was seized, and with it the false prophet, who had performed before it the signs by which he deceived those who received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped its image; the two were cast alive into the lake of fire that burns with sulfur.
verses.note: “Was seized”: Gr. ἐπιάσθη. “The false prophet”: cf. 13:11–17; 16:13. “Lake of fire that burns with sulfur”: cf. 14:10; 20:10, 14–15; 21:8; Dan 7:11.

verses.text: The rest were killed with the sword that came out of the mouth of Him who sat on the horse; and all the birds were filled with their flesh.
verses.note: “The rest”: Gr. οἱ λοιποί (cf. 9:20). “Came out”: Gr. ἐξελθούσῃ, aorist; the Textus Receptus reads “comes out”. “Were filled”: cf. Ezek 39:4, 17–20.

segments.text: After these things I heard as it were a loud voice of a great multitude in heaven, saying:
Hallelujah!
Salvation, and glory, and power belong to our God,
because true and just are His judgments;
because He has judged the great prostitute,
who corrupted the earth with her prostitution,
and He has avenged the blood of His servants at her hand.
And they said a second time:
Hallelujah!
And her smoke goes up forever and ever.
And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God, who is seated on the throne, saying:
Amen! Hallelujah!
And a voice came out from the throne, saying:
Praise our God, all His servants,
and you who fear Him, the small and the great.
And I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude, and as it were the voice of many waters, and as it were the voice of mighty thunders, saying:
Hallelujah!
For the Lord God, the Almighty, has begun to reign.
Let us rejoice and exult,
and we will give Him the glory,
because the wedding of the Lamb has come,
and His wife has made herself ready;
and it was granted to her to clothe herself in fine linen, bright and pure; for the fine linen is the righteous acts of the saints.
Then he says to me: Write: Blessed are those who have been called to the wedding supper of the Lamb. And he says to me: These words are true words of God.

And I fell down before his feet to worship him. And he says to me: See that you do not do that; I am a fellow servant of yours and of your brothers who have the Testimony of Jesus. Worship God; for the Testimony of Jesus is the Spirit of prophecy.

blocks.text: The Rider on the white horse

segments.text: And I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse, and He who sat on it is called Faithful and True, and in righteousness He judges and makes war.
His eyes are a flame of fire, and on His head are many diadems, and He has a name written that no one knows except He Himself;
and He is clothed in a garment dipped in blood; and His name is called: the Word of God.
The armies that are in heaven followed Him on white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and pure.

From His mouth comes a sharp sword, so that with it He may strike the nations; and He will shepherd them with a rod of iron; and He treads the winepress of the wine of the fury of the wrath of God, the Almighty.
He has on His garment and on His thigh a name written: King of kings and Lord of lords.
And I saw an angel standing in the sun, and he cried out with a loud voice, saying to all the birds that fly in midheaven: Come, gather together for the great supper of God,
to eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of commanders, and the flesh of mighty men, and the flesh of horses and of those who sit on them, and the flesh of all, free and slaves, and small and great.
And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered to make the war against Him who sat on the horse and against His army.

Then the beast was seized, and with it the false prophet, who had performed before it the signs by which he deceived those who received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped its image; the two were cast alive into the lake of fire that burns with sulfur.
The rest were killed with the sword that came out of the mouth of Him who sat on the horse; and all the birds were filled with their flesh.

headings.text: The judgment before the great white throne

verses.text: And I saw an angel coming down from heaven, having the key of the abyss and a great chain in his hand.
verses.note: “The key of the abyss”: cf. 1:18; 9:1. “Abyss”: Gr. ἄβυσσος, the same word as in the LXX of Gen 1:2. Cf. Jer 4:23–26. “Chain”: Gr. ἅλυσις.

verses.text: He seized the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years,
verses.note: “Seized”: Gr. ἐκράτησεν. “The ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan”: cf. 12:9; Gen 3:1. “A thousand years”: Gr. χίλια ἔτη (cf. 20:3–7). “Bound him”: cf. Isa 24:21–22; Matt 12:29. Variant: the Byzantine text adds “who deceives the whole world”.

verses.text: and cast him into the abyss, and shut and sealed it over him, so that he would no longer deceive the nations, until the thousand years were completed; after these things he must be released for a little while.
verses.note: “Shut and sealed it over him”: Gr. ἔκλεισεν καὶ ἐσφράγισεν ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ, that is, the abyss (cf. Dan 6:17 (Heb. 6:18); Matt 27:66); the Textus Receptus reads “shut him”. “Deceive”: Gr. πλανάω (cf. 12:9; 20:8, 10). “Were completed”: Gr. τελεσθῇ (cf. 17:17; 20:5, 7). “A little while”: Gr. μικρὸν χρόνον (cf. 6:11).

verses.text: And I saw thrones, and they sat on them, and judgment was given to them; and I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded because of the Testimony of Jesus and because of the Word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast or its image, and had not received the mark on their forehead and on their hand; and they came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years.
verses.note: “Thrones… judgment”: Gr. κρίμα (cf. Dan 7:9, 22, 26; Matt 19:28; 1 Cor 6:2–3). “And I saw the souls”: “I saw” is implied in the Greek. “The souls”: Gr. ψυχαί (cf. 6:9). “Beheaded”: Gr. πεπελεκισμένων, lit. “beheaded with an axe”. “The Testimony of Jesus… the Word of God”: cf. 1:2, 9; 6:9; 12:17. “Mark”: cf. 13:16–17; 14:9. “Came to life”: Gr. ἔζησαν, lit. “lived”, an ingressive aorist, “began to live” (cf. 2:8; 13:14; Ezek 37:10). “Christ”: Gr. τοῦ χριστοῦ, with the article, “the Christ”; the Textus Receptus omits the article.

verses.text: The rest of the dead did not come to life until the thousand years were completed. This is the first resurrection.
verses.note: “The rest of the dead”: Gr. οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν νεκρῶν. “Did not come to life”: lit. “did not live” (cf. 20:4); the Textus Receptus reads ἀνέζησαν. Variant: Codex Sinaiticus and part of the Byzantine tradition omit the first sentence of the verse. “The first resurrection”: cf. John 5:28–29; 1 Thess 4:16; Luke 14:14.

verses.text: Blessed and holy is the one who has part in the first resurrection; over these the second death has no authority, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and will reign with Him for a thousand years.
verses.note: “Blessed”: cf. 1:3; 14:13; 19:9. “The second death”: cf. 2:11; 20:14; 21:8. “Priests of God and of Christ”: cf. 1:6; 5:10; Ex 19:6. “Will reign with Him for a thousand years”: cf. 5:10; 22:5.

verses.text: When the thousand years are completed, Satan will be released from his prison,
verses.note: “Prison”: Gr. φυλακή (cf. 2:10; 18:2).

verses.text: and will go out to deceive the nations that are at the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them for the war; their number is like the sand of the sea.
verses.note: “The four corners of the earth”: cf. 7:1. “Gog and Magog”: cf. Ezek 38–39. “For the war”: Gr. τὸν πόλεμον (cf. 16:14; 19:19); the Textus Receptus omits the article. “Like the sand of the sea”: cf. Gen 22:17; Josh 11:4.

verses.text: They went up over the breadth of the earth, and surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city; and fire came down from heaven and devoured them.
verses.note: “The breadth of the earth”: Gr. τὸ πλάτος τῆς γῆς (cf. Hab 1:6). “Over the breadth of the earth”: lit. “upon the breadth of the earth”. “Camp”: Gr. παρεμβολή. “The beloved city”: cf. Ps 87:2 [LXX 86:2]; Jer 11:15. “Fire came down from heaven”: cf. 2 Kgs 1:10–12; Ezek 38:22; 39:6; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus add “from God”.

verses.text: The devil, who deceived them, was cast into the lake of fire and sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet also are; and they will be tormented day and night forever and ever.
verses.note: “The lake of fire and sulfur”: cf. 19:20; 21:8. “Will be tormented”: Gr. βασανίζω (cf. 14:10–11). “Forever and ever”: cf. 14:11; Isa 34:9–10; Jude 7.

verses.text: And I saw a great white throne and Him who sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away, and no place was found for them.
verses.note: “Great white throne”: cf. Dan 7:9–10. “From whose face the earth and the heaven fled away”: cf. 6:14; 16:20; 21:1; Ps 102:25–26 (Heb. 102:26–27) [LXX 101:26–27]; 2 Pet 3:10.

verses.text: And I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne; and books were opened; and another book was opened, which is the book of life; and the dead were judged by the things that were written in the books, according to their works.
verses.note: “The great and the small”: cf. 11:18; 19:5. “Books were opened”: cf. Dan 7:10; 12:1; Mal 3:16. “Which is the book of life”: lit. “which is of life” (cf. 3:5; 13:8; 17:8; 21:27). “According to their works”: cf. 2:23; 22:12; Ps 62:12 (Heb. 62:13) [LXX 61:13]; Rom 2:6. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “before God” instead of “before the throne”, and “small and great”.

verses.text: The sea gave up the dead who were in it, and death and the grave gave up the dead who were in them; and they were judged, each one according to their works.
verses.note: “Death and the grave”: Gr. ὁ θάνατος καὶ ὁ ᾅδης (cf. 1:18; 6:8). “Each one”: Gr. ἕκαστος.

verses.text: Then death and the grave were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire.
verses.note: “The second death, the lake of fire”: cf. 2:11; 20:6; 21:8; Isa 25:8; 1 Cor 15:26; the Textus Receptus omits “the lake of fire”.

verses.text: If anyone was not found written in the book of life, he was cast into the lake of fire.
verses.note: “Book of life”: Gr. ἡ βίβλος τῆς ζωῆς (cf. 3:5; 13:8; Dan 12:1).

segments.text: And I saw an angel coming down from heaven, having the key of the abyss and a great chain in his hand.
He seized the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years,

and cast him into the abyss, and shut and sealed it over him, so that he would no longer deceive the nations, until the thousand years were completed; after these things he must be released for a little while.

And I saw thrones, and they sat on them, and judgment was given to them; and I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded because of the Testimony of Jesus and because of the Word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast or its image, and had not received the mark on their forehead and on their hand; and they came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years.
The rest of the dead did not come to life until the thousand years were completed. This is the first resurrection.

Blessed and holy is the one who has part in the first resurrection; over these the second death has no authority, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and will reign with Him for a thousand years.
When the thousand years are completed, Satan will be released from his prison,
and will go out to deceive the nations that are at the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them for the war; their number is like the sand of the sea.
They went up over the breadth of the earth, and surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city; and fire came down from heaven and devoured them.
The devil, who deceived them, was cast into the lake of fire and sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet also are; and they will be tormented day and night forever and ever.

blocks.text: The judgment before the great white throne

segments.text: And I saw a great white throne and Him who sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away, and no place was found for them.

And I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne; and books were opened; and another book was opened, which is the book of life; and the dead were judged by the things that were written in the books, according to their works.
The sea gave up the dead who were in it, and death and the grave gave up the dead who were in them; and they were judged, each one according to their works.
Then death and the grave were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire.
If anyone was not found written in the book of life, he was cast into the lake of fire.

headings.text: The new heaven and the new earth

verses.text: And I saw a new heaven and a new earth; for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea is no more.
verses.note: “A new heaven and a new earth”: Gr. καινός, “new” in quality (cf. 2:17; 3:12; 5:9; Isa 65:17; 66:22; 2 Pet 3:13). “Had passed away”: Gr. ἀπῆλθαν, lit. “went away” (cf. 20:11; 21:4); the Textus Receptus reads παρῆλθε. “The sea is no more”: cf. 13:1; 20:13. Variant: Codex Alexandrinus reads “and the sea I saw no more”.

verses.text: And I saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
verses.note: “The holy city, the new Jerusalem”: cf. 3:12; 11:2; Isa 52:1; Heb 11:10, 16; 12:22. “From God”: Gr. ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ (cf. 3:12; 21:10). “Bride”: Gr. νύμφη (cf. 18:23; 21:9; 22:17). “Adorned”: Gr. κοσμέω (cf. 21:19; Isa 61:10). Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “And I, John, saw the holy city”.

verses.text: And I heard a loud voice from the throne, saying: Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and He will have His tabernacle with them, and they will be His peoples, and God Himself will be with them,
verses.note: “From the throne”: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “from heaven”. “Tabernacle… have His tabernacle”: Gr. σκηνή… σκηνώσει (cf. 7:15; 12:12; 13:6; John 1:14); an echo of Lev 26:11–12 and Ezek 37:27. “His peoples”: Gr. λαοί, plural (cf. Zech 2:11 (Heb. 2:15)); the Byzantine text reads the singular, “His people”. Variant: Codex Alexandrinus and the Textus Receptus add “their God” at the end of the verse.

verses.text: and He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death will be no more, nor will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain anymore; the first things have passed away.
verses.note: “Wipe away every tear”: cf. 7:17; Isa 25:8. “Death will be no more”: cf. 20:14; 1 Cor 15:26, 54. “Mourning”: Gr. πένθος (cf. 18:7–8). “Crying”: Gr. κραυγή, lit. “outcry, shout”. “Pain”: Gr. πόνος (cf. 16:10–11). “The first things have passed away”: cf. Isa 43:18–19; 65:16–17; 2 Cor 5:17. Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “for the first things have passed away”; the Textus Receptus adds “God” after “will wipe away”.

verses.text: And He who is seated on the throne said: Behold, I make all things new. And He says: Write, for these words are faithful and true.
verses.note: “Behold, I make all things new”: Gr. καινὰ ποιῶ πάντα (cf. Isa 43:19). “And He says”: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus add “to me”. “Faithful and true”: cf. 3:14; 19:9, 11; 22:6; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “true and faithful”.

verses.text: And He said to me: It is done! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End. To the one who is thirsty I will give freely from the spring of the water of life.
verses.note: “It is done”: Gr. γέγοναν, perfect plural, lit. “They are done”, referring to “all things” in v. 5 (cf. 16:17). Variants: Codex Sinaiticus and the Byzantine text read γέγονα; the Textus Receptus reads the singular γέγονε. “The Alpha and the Omega”: cf. 1:8; 22:13. “The Beginning and the End”: Gr. ἡ ἀρχὴ καὶ τὸ τέλος (cf. 3:14; 22:13; Isa 44:6). “To the one who is thirsty… freely”: Gr. δωρεάν (cf. 7:16–17; 22:17; Isa 55:1; John 4:10, 14).

verses.text: The one who conquers will inherit these things, and I will be his God, and he will be My son.
verses.note: “The one who conquers”: cf. 2:7, 11, 17, 26; 3:5, 12, 21. “Will inherit these things”: the Textus Receptus reads “will inherit all things”. “I will be his God, and he will be My son”: lit. “I will be God to him, and he will be son to Me” (cf. 2 Sam 7:14; Ps 89:26–27 (Heb. 89:27–28) [LXX 88:27–28]; Jer 31:33 [LXX 38:33]).

verses.text: But as for the cowardly, and unfaithful, and abominable, and murderers, and the immoral, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, their part will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur, which is the second death.
verses.note: “Unfaithful”: Gr. ἄπιστοι, in contrast with the “faithful” (πιστοί) words of v. 5; or “unbelieving”. “Abominable”: Gr. ἐβδελυγμένοι, “those who have become abominable” (cf. 17:4–5; 21:27). “Murderers”: Gr. φονεῖς (cf. 9:21). “The immoral”: Gr. πόρνοι, those who practice prostitution, πορνεία (cf. 2:14, 20–21; 22:15). “Sorcerers”: Gr. φάρμακοι (cf. 9:21; 18:23; 22:15). “The second death”: cf. 2:11; 20:6, 14. Variant: the Byzantine text adds “and sinners” after “unfaithful”.

verses.text: And one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls full of the seven last plagues came and spoke with me, saying: Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb.
verses.note: “One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls”: cf. 15:1, 7; 17:1. “Full”: Gr. γεμόντων, which in the Greek agrees with “angels”; rendered by the sense, as in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus, which make it agree with “bowls” (γεμούσας). “The bride, the wife of the Lamb”: cf. 19:7–8; 21:2. The phrase mirrors 17:1: the bride-city in contrast with the prostitute-city.

verses.text: And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God,
verses.note: “Carried me away in the Spirit”: Gr. ἀπήνεγκέν με ἐν πνεύματι, as in 17:3 (cf. 1:10; 4:2). “A great and high mountain”: cf. Ezek 40:2; Isa 2:2. “The holy city, Jerusalem”: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “the great city, the holy Jerusalem”.

verses.text: having the glory of God; its radiance was like a most precious stone, like a jasper stone, clear as crystal;
verses.note: “The glory of God”: cf. 15:8; 21:23; Isa 60:1–2; Ezek 43:2–5. “Radiance”: Gr. φωστήρ, “luminary, brilliance”. “Jasper”: cf. 4:3; 21:18–19. “Clear as crystal”: Gr. κρυσταλλίζω, “to shine like crystal” (cf. 4:6; 22:1).

verses.text: having a great and high wall, having twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names inscribed, which are those of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel:
verses.note: “Gates”: Gr. πυλών, the gate with its gateway (cf. 22:14). “Names inscribed… of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel”: cf. 7:4–8; Ezek 48:30–34; Ex 28:21.

verses.text: on the east, three gates; and on the north, three gates; and on the south, three gates; and on the west, three gates.
verses.note: “On the east… on the west”: lit. “from the rising… from the setting” (cf. Ezek 48:31–34; Luke 13:29).

verses.text: The wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
verses.note: “Foundations”: Gr. θεμέλιοι (cf. Heb 11:10; Eph 2:20). “Twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb”: cf. Matt 10:2; the Textus Receptus reads “and in them the names”.

verses.text: The one who spoke with me had as a measure a golden reed, to measure the city, and its gates, and its wall.
verses.note: “Reed”: Gr. κάλαμος, a measuring reed (cf. 11:1; Ezek 40:3, 5; Zech 2:1–2 (Heb. 2:5–6)). “As a measure”: Gr. μέτρον; the Textus Receptus omits it.

verses.text: The city lies foursquare, and its length is as great as its width. And he measured the city with the reed: twelve thousand stadia; its length, and width, and height are equal.
verses.note: “Lies foursquare”: Gr. τετράγωνος κεῖται (cf. Ezek 43:16; 48:16–20); equal in length, width and height, like the Most Holy Place (1 Kgs 6:20). “Twelve thousand stadia”: about 2,220 kilometers (1,380 miles); one stadion, about 185 meters (607 feet) (cf. 14:20). The number 12 × 1,000 takes up 7:4–8.

verses.text: And he measured its wall: one hundred and forty-four cubits, by a man’s measure, which is the angel’s.
verses.note: “One hundred and forty-four cubits”: about 65 meters (216 feet); one cubit, about 45 centimeters (18 inches). The number 12 × 12 takes up 7:4; 14:1. It is not said whether the measure is the height or the thickness of the wall. “By a man’s measure, which is the angel’s”: that is, the angel used the ordinary human measure.

verses.text: The material of its wall was jasper, and the city was pure gold, like pure glass.
verses.note: “Material”: Gr. ἐνδώμησις, “structure, building material”. “Pure gold, like pure glass”: Gr. καθαρός in both expressions (cf. 21:21).

verses.text: The foundations of the wall of the city were adorned with every kind of precious stone: the first foundation, jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, chalcedony; the fourth, emerald;
verses.note: “Adorned”: Gr. κοσμέω (cf. 21:2). “Every kind of precious stone”: Gr. παντὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ, lit. “every precious stone”; cf. Ex 28:17–20; Isa 54:11–12; Ezek 28:13. The twelve stones correspond, broadly, to those of the high priest’s breastpiece. “Sapphire”: Gr. σάπφιρος, probably lapis lazuli.

verses.text: the fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, topaz; the tenth, chrysoprase; the eleventh, jacinth; the twelfth, amethyst.
verses.note: The exact identification of some stones is uncertain. “Sardonyx”: Gr. σαρδόνυξ. “Sardius”: Gr. σάρδιον (cf. 4:3). “Chrysolite”: Gr. χρυσόλιθος, lit. “gold stone”. “Chrysoprase”: Gr. χρυσόπρασος, a golden-green stone. “Jacinth”: Gr. ὑάκινθος (cf. 9:17).

verses.text: The twelve gates were twelve pearls; each of the gates was of a single pearl. The street of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass.
verses.note: “Pearls”: Gr. μαργαρῖται (cf. 17:4; 18:12, 16; Matt 13:45–46). “Street”: Gr. πλατεῖα, the main street (cf. 11:8; 22:2). “Transparent glass”: Gr. ὕαλος διαυγής; the Textus Receptus reads διαφανής.

verses.text: And I saw no sanctuary in it, for the Lord God, the Almighty, is its sanctuary, and the Lamb.
verses.note: “Sanctuary”: Gr. ναός (cf. 3:12; 7:15; 11:19). The sanctuary of the city is the presence of God and of the Lamb (cf. 21:3; 22:3–4; John 2:19–21), and the city itself has the cubic form of the Most Holy Place (cf. 21:16; 1 Kgs 6:20). Alternative reading: the verse stresses the primacy of the divine presence, before which any structure becomes secondary. “The Lord God, the Almighty”: cf. 1:8; 4:8; 11:17; 15:3.

verses.text: The city has no need of the sun, nor of the moon, to shine on it, for the glory of God has illuminated it, and its lamp is the Lamb.
verses.note: “No need of the sun, nor of the moon”: cf. 22:5; Isa 60:19–20. “Has illuminated it”: Gr. ἐφώτισεν, aorist. “Its lamp is the Lamb”: Gr. λύχνος (cf. 18:23; 22:5; John 8:12).

verses.text: The nations will walk by its light; and the kings of the earth bring their glory into it.
verses.note: “The nations will walk by its light”: Gr. διὰ τοῦ φωτὸς αὐτῆς, lit. “through its light” (cf. Isa 60:3, 5, 11). “Their glory”: Gr. αὐτῶν, the glory of the kings. “Bring”: present in the Greek. Variants: the Byzantine text reads “bring to it glory and honor of the nations”; the Textus Receptus reads “the nations of those who are saved will walk in its light” and “their glory and honor”.

verses.text: Its gates will never be shut by day, for there will be no night there;
verses.note: “Will never be shut by day”: Gr. οὐ μὴ κλεισθῶσιν (cf. Isa 60:11; Zech 14:7). “There will be no night”: cf. 22:5.

verses.text: and they will bring into it the glory and the honor of the nations.
verses.note: “The glory and the honor of the nations”: cf. Isa 60:5, 11; 66:12.

verses.text: And nothing profane will ever enter it, nor anyone who practices abomination and falsehood, but only those who are written in the book of life of the Lamb.
verses.note: “Nothing profane”: Gr. πᾶν κοινόν, “everything common, profane”; the Textus Receptus reads κοινοῦν, “that which defiles”. “Abomination and falsehood”: cf. 21:8; 22:15. “Written in the book of life of the Lamb”: cf. 3:5; 13:8; 17:8; 20:12, 15; Isa 52:1; Ezek 44:9.

blocks.text: The new heaven and the new earth

segments.text: And I saw a new heaven and a new earth; for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea is no more.
And I saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
And I heard a loud voice from the throne, saying:
Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men,
and He will have His tabernacle with them,
and they will be His peoples,
and God Himself will be with them,
and He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,
and death will be no more,
nor will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain anymore;
the first things have passed away.
And He who is seated on the throne said: Behold, I make all things new. And He says: Write, for these words are faithful and true.
And He said to me: It is done! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End. To the one who is thirsty I will give freely from the spring of the water of life.
The one who conquers will inherit these things, and I will be his God, and he will be My son.

But as for the cowardly, and unfaithful, and abominable, and murderers, and the immoral, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, their part will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur, which is the second death.
And one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls full of the seven last plagues came and spoke with me, saying: Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb.
And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God,
having the glory of God; its radiance was like a most precious stone, like a jasper stone, clear as crystal;
having a great and high wall, having twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names inscribed, which are those of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel:
on the east, three gates; and on the north, three gates; and on the south, three gates; and on the west, three gates.
The wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
The one who spoke with me had as a measure a golden reed, to measure the city, and its gates, and its wall.
The city lies foursquare, and its length is as great as its width. And he measured the city with the reed: twelve thousand stadia; its length, and width, and height are equal.
And he measured its wall: one hundred and forty-four cubits, by a man’s measure, which is the angel’s.
The material of its wall was jasper, and the city was pure gold, like pure glass.
The foundations of the wall of the city were adorned with every kind of precious stone: the first foundation, jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, chalcedony; the fourth, emerald;
the fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, topaz; the tenth, chrysoprase; the eleventh, jacinth; the twelfth, amethyst.
The twelve gates were twelve pearls; each of the gates was of a single pearl. The street of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass.
And I saw no sanctuary in it, for the Lord God, the Almighty, is its sanctuary, and the Lamb.
The city has no need of the sun, nor of the moon, to shine on it, for the glory of God has illuminated it, and its lamp is the Lamb.
The nations will walk by its light; and the kings of the earth bring their glory into it.
Its gates will never be shut by day, for there will be no night there;
and they will bring into it the glory and the honor of the nations.
And nothing profane will ever enter it, nor anyone who practices abomination and falsehood, but only those who are written in the book of life of the Lamb.

headings.text: The river of the water of life

verses.text: And he showed me a river of the water of life, bright as crystal, coming out from the throne of God and of the Lamb,
verses.note: “River of the water of life”: cf. 7:17; 21:6; Ezek 47:1–12; Zech 14:8; Ps 46:4 (Heb. 46:5) [LXX 45:5]; John 7:38. “Bright”: Gr. λαμπρός (cf. 15:6; 19:8). “Coming out”: Gr. ἐκπορεύομαι. Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “a pure river of the water of life”.

verses.text: in the middle of its street. On either side of the river is the tree of life, producing twelve fruits, yielding its fruit every month; and the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations.
verses.note: “Street”: Gr. πλατεῖα (cf. 21:21). “On either side of the river”: Gr. ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ἐκεῖθεν (cf. Ezek 47:7, 12). “The tree of life”: Gr. ξύλον ζωῆς, possibly collective, “trees” (cf. 2:7; 22:14, 19; Gen 2:9; 3:22–24). “Every month”: lit. “according to each month”. “Healing”: Gr. θεραπεία (cf. Ezek 47:12).

verses.text: There will no longer be any curse. And the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and His servants will serve Him,
verses.note: “Curse”: Gr. κατάθεμα, “accursed thing” (cf. Gen 3:17; Zech 14:11); the Textus Receptus reads κατανάθεμα. “The throne of God and of the Lamb”: cf. 3:21; 7:17. “His servants will serve Him”: Gr. αὐτοῦ… αὐτῷ, singular, referring to God and the Lamb together (cf. 11:15; 20:6). “Serve”: Gr. λατρεύω, to serve in worship (cf. 7:15).

verses.text: and they will see His face, and His name will be on their foreheads.
verses.note: “They will see His face”: cf. Ex 33:20, 23; Ps 17:15 [LXX 16:15]; Matt 5:8; 1 Cor 13:12; 1 John 3:2. “His name… on their foreheads”: cf. 3:12; 7:3; 14:1, in contrast with 13:16–17.

verses.text: There will be no more night, and they have no need of the light of a lamp or the light of the sun, for the Lord God will shine on them; and they will reign forever and ever.
verses.note: “There will be no more night”: cf. 21:25; Zech 14:7. “Have no need”: present in the Greek (cf. 21:23). “Will shine on them”: Gr. φωτίσει ἐπ’ αὐτούς, lit. “will give light upon them” (cf. Isa 60:19–20; Num 6:25). “Will reign”: cf. 5:10; 20:4, 6; Dan 7:18, 27. Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “there will be no night there” and “need of a lamp”; the Textus Receptus reads “gives them light”.

verses.text: And he said to me: These words are faithful and true; and the Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, has sent His angel to show His servants the things that must soon happen.
verses.note: “Faithful and true”: cf. 19:9; 21:5. “The God of the spirits of the prophets”: cf. Num 27:16; 1 Cor 14:32; the Textus Receptus reads “the God of the holy prophets”; the Byzantine text reads “And he says to me”. “To show His servants the things that must soon happen”: takes up 1:1 and frames the book.

verses.text: And behold, I am coming soon. Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.
verses.note: “Behold, I am coming soon”: cf. 2:16; 3:11; 22:12, 20. “Blessed”: cf. 1:3; 14:13; 16:15; 19:9; 20:6; 22:14, the sixth of the seven beatitudes of the book. “Keeps”: Gr. τηρέω (cf. 1:3; 3:10; 12:17; 14:12).

verses.text: And I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. When I heard and saw, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel who showed me these things.
verses.note: “Am the one who heard and saw”: Gr. ὁ ἀκούων καὶ βλέπων, present participles, lit. “the one who hears and sees” (cf. 1:1, 4, 9). “I fell down to worship”: cf. 19:10.

verses.text: And he says to me: See that you do not do that; I am a fellow servant of yours and of your brothers the prophets, and of those who keep the words of this book. Worship God.
verses.note: “See that you do not do that”: Gr. ὅρα μή (cf. 19:10). “Fellow servant”: Gr. σύνδουλος (cf. 6:11; 19:10). “The prophets, and of those who keep the words of this book”: cf. 19:10. “Worship God”: cf. 14:7.

verses.text: And he says to me: Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near.
verses.note: “Do not seal up”: in contrast with Dan 8:26; 12:4, 9 (cf. 10:4). “The time is near”: Gr. ὁ καιρὸς ἐγγύς (cf. 1:3).

verses.text: Let the one who does wrong still do wrong; and the filthy still be filthy; and the righteous still do righteousness; and the holy still be made holy.
verses.note: “The one who does wrong”: Gr. ὁ ἀδικῶν, “the one who practices injustice”; the same verb is “harm” in 2:11; 7:2–3. “Still”: Gr. ἔτι, “let him continue”. Cf. Dan 12:10; Ezek 3:27. “Be made holy”: Gr. ἁγιασθήτω (cf. Lev 11:44). Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “and the righteous, let him be made righteous still”.

verses.text: Behold, I am coming soon, and My reward is with Me, to repay each one according to his work.
verses.note: “Reward”: Gr. μισθός (cf. 11:18; Isa 40:10; 62:11). “To repay each one according to his work”: lit. “as his work is” (cf. 2:23; 20:12–13; Ps 62:12 (Heb. 62:13) [LXX 61:13]; Prov 24:12; Matt 16:27; Rom 2:6). Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “as his work will be”.

verses.text: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End.
verses.note: “The Alpha and the Omega”: cf. 1:8; 21:6. “The First and the Last”: cf. 1:17; 2:8; Isa 44:6; 48:12. “The Beginning and the End”: cf. 3:14; 21:6. Titles of God in 1:8 and 21:6, here on the lips of Jesus (cf. 22:16). Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “the Beginning and the End, the First and the Last”.

verses.text: Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they may have the right to the tree of life and may enter the city by the gates.
verses.note: “Blessed”: the seventh of the seven beatitudes of the book (cf. 1:3; 14:13; 16:15; 19:9; 20:6; 22:7). “Those who wash their robes”: Gr. οἱ πλύνοντες τὰς στολὰς αὐτῶν (cf. 7:14; 3:4–5; 19:8); the reading of Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Alexandrinus. Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “those who do His commandments”, Gr. οἱ ποιοῦντες τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ (cf. 12:17; 14:12; John 14:15; 1 John 5:3). In Greek capital letters the two readings look very much alike. “Right”: Gr. ἐξουσία, “authority, right” (cf. 2:7; 22:2, 19). “By the gates”: cf. 21:12, 25, 27; Ps 118:19–20 [LXX 117:19–20]; Gen 3:24.

verses.text: Outside are the dogs, and the sorcerers, and the immoral, and the murderers, and the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.
verses.note: “Outside”: cf. 21:8, 27; Matt 8:12. “Dogs”: an image of the impure (cf. Deut 23:18 (Heb. 23:19); Phil 3:2). “Sorcerers… immoral… murderers… idolaters”: cf. 21:8. “Who loves and practices falsehood”: cf. 14:5; 21:27; 2 Thess 2:10–12.

verses.text: I, Jesus, have sent My angel to testify these things to you for the churches. I am the Root and the Offspring of David, the bright Morning Star.
verses.note: “I, Jesus”: cf. 1:1. “For the churches”: Gr. ἐπὶ ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις, also “to the churches” or “concerning the churches”. “The Root and the Offspring of David”: cf. 5:5; Isa 11:1, 10; Rom 1:3. “The bright Morning Star”: cf. 2:28; Num 24:17; 2 Pet 1:19. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “the bright and morning Star”.

verses.text: And the Spirit and the bride say: Come! And let the one who hears say: Come! And let the one who is thirsty come; let whoever wishes take the water of life freely.
verses.note: “The Spirit”: cf. 2:7; 14:13. “The bride”: cf. 21:2, 9. “Come!”: Gr. ἔρχου (cf. 22:20). “The one who is thirsty… freely”: cf. 21:6; Isa 55:1; John 7:37. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “and whoever wishes”.

verses.text: I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: if anyone adds to them, God will add to him the plagues that are written in this book;
verses.note: “I testify”: Gr. μαρτυρῶ (cf. 1:2); the Textus Receptus reads “For I testify together”. “If anyone adds to them”: cf. Deut 4:2; 12:32 (Heb. 13:1); Prov 30:6 [LXX 24:29]. “The plagues”: cf. 15:1, 6; 16:1–21; Deut 29:20 (Heb. 29:19). Variant: the Byzantine text reads “may God add” (and, in v. 19, “may God take away”).

verses.text: and if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God will take away his part from the tree of life and from the holy city, which are written in this book.
verses.note: “Takes away”: Gr. ἀφαιρέω (cf. Deut 4:2). “His part from the tree of life”: cf. 2:7; 22:2, 14. Variant: the Textus Receptus reads “from the book of life”, a reading without support in the ancient Greek manuscripts (cf. 3:5; 20:12).

verses.text: He who testifies to these things says: Yes, I am coming soon. Amen. Come, Lord Jesus!
verses.note: “He who testifies”: cf. 1:2, 5; 3:14. “Yes”: Gr. ναί (cf. 1:7; 14:13; 16:7). “Come, Lord Jesus”: Gr. ἔρχου, κύριε Ἰησοῦ, the Greek equivalent of the Aramaic Maranatha (cf. 1 Cor 16:22). Variant: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read “Amen. Yes, come, Lord Jesus”.

verses.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all. Amen.
verses.note: “The grace… be with all”: cf. 1:4; 2 Thess 3:18. “Amen”: with Codex Sinaiticus, the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus; Codex Alexandrinus omits it. Variants: Codex Sinaiticus reads “with the saints”; the Byzantine text reads “of the Lord Jesus Christ with all the saints”; the Textus Receptus reads “of our Lord Jesus Christ with you all”.

blocks.text: The river of the water of life

segments.text: And he showed me a river of the water of life, bright as crystal, coming out from the throne of God and of the Lamb,
in the middle of its street. On either side of the river is the tree of life, producing twelve fruits, yielding its fruit every month; and the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations.
There will no longer be any curse. And the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and His servants will serve Him,
and they will see His face, and His name will be on their foreheads.
There will be no more night, and they have no need of the light of a lamp or the light of the sun, for the Lord God will shine on them; and they will reign forever and ever.
And he said to me: These words are faithful and true; and the Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, has sent His angel to show His servants the things that must soon happen.
And behold, I am coming soon. Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.
And I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. When I heard and saw, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel who showed me these things.
And he says to me: See that you do not do that; I am a fellow servant of yours and of your brothers the prophets, and of those who keep the words of this book. Worship God.
And he says to me: Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near.
Let the one who does wrong still do wrong; and the filthy still be filthy; and the righteous still do righteousness; and the holy still be made holy.
Behold, I am coming soon, and My reward is with Me, to repay each one according to his work.
I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End.
Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they may have the right to the tree of life and may enter the city by the gates.
Outside are the dogs, and the sorcerers, and the immoral, and the murderers, and the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.
I, Jesus, have sent My angel to testify these things to you for the churches. I am the Root and the Offspring of David, the bright Morning Star.
And the Spirit and the bride say: Come! And let the one who hears say: Come! And let the one who is thirsty come; let whoever wishes take the water of life freely.
I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: if anyone adds to them, God will add to him the plagues that are written in this book;
and if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God will take away his part from the tree of life and from the holy city, which are written in this book.
He who testifies to these things says: Yes, I am coming soon. Amen. Come, Lord Jesus!
The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all. Amen.
